The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿and his wives﴾ is that it covers everyone who is described as being his wife, peace be upon him, whether he divorced her or did not divorce her. It has been said: this ruling does not apply to a divorced woman. It has also been said: whoever he consummated the marriage with, her prohibition is established with certainty. Umar intended to stone a woman whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had separated from, and who had married again afterward. She said to him: "Why this? He did not place a veil upon me, nor was I named a mother to the Muslims." So he refrained from her. At first in Medina there was inheritance by the brotherhood of Islam and by emigration, then Allah, the Exalted, ruled that blood relatives (ulu al-arham) have a better claim to inheritance than the brother in Islam, or by emigration, in the Book of Allah, i.e., in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), or in the Qur'an, of (p-213) the believers and the emigrants. That is, they are closer than the believers, who used to inherit merely by faith, and than the emigrants, who used to inherit by emigration. This is the apparent meaning, so the *min* (from) here is like the *min* in: "Zayd is better than Amr." Al-Zamakhshari said: it is permissible that it be an explanation of "blood relatives," meaning: the relatives, some of whom are closer than others to inherit from one another than strangers. End of quote. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿to your allies﴾ is general, so it includes all its categories, whether relative or stranger, believer or disbeliever, to whom one shows kindness and whom one joins in life, and to whom one bequeaths at death. This was said by Qatadah, al-Hasan, Ata', and Ibn al-Hanafiyyah. Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, al-Rummani and others said: ﴿to your allies﴾ is specific to the believers.

The context of what preceded concerning the believers supports this. However, the bond of kinship is not removed from the disbeliever; what is removed is that one should cast affection toward him, like a guardian of Islam. This exception in His saying ﴿except that you do﴾ is something understood from the speech, meaning: ﴿blood relatives are closer to one another﴾ in benefit by inheritance and other things. It is transitive with *ila* (to) because the meaning is: "except that you give to your allies," which is an allusion to what is in the two verses. (In the Book) is either the Preserved Tablet or the Qur'an, as previously mentioned.

﴿Written﴾, i.e., inscribed in writing. This sentence is a new independent clause, like a conclusion to what has been mentioned of rulings. Since what preceded were rulings from Allah, the Exalted, and among them were matters from the pre-Islamic period and matters in Islam that were abrogated (naskh), He followed it with His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾, i.e., to convey the laws and to call to Allah. So you are not an innovator in conveying from Allah. The governing element of *idh* (when), as stated by al-Hawfi and Ibn Atiyyah, may be (written), i.e., written in the Mother of the Book, and at the time when We took. It has been said: the governing element is "remember when We took." This covenant concerns conveying the messages of Allah and calling to faith, and no obstacle prevents them from it, neither fear nor desire. Al-Kalbi said: their covenant was taken to convey. Qatadah said: it was to confirm one another's truthfulness, to announce that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and for the Messenger of Allah to announce that there is no prophet after him. Al-Zajjaj and others said: what was taken from them was at the time of the extraction of the offspring of Adam from his loins like particles. They said: then Allah took at that time the covenant of the prophets to convey and to confirm one another, and to all that prophethood encompasses. Something similar was narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. These five were singled out for mention after being included among the prophets. It has been said: they are the Ulu al-'Azm (the prophets of firm resolve), due to their nobility and excellence over others. Muhammad was placed first because he is more excellent than them and has more followers. Noah was placed first in the verse of al-Shura, in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ (Qur'an 42:13), because its presentation there is different. There, it was presented as a description of the religion of Islam as the original religion, as if He said: He has legislated for you the original religion with which Noah was sent in the old covenant, with which Muhammad was sent, seal of the prophets, in the new covenant, and with which were sent the well-known prophets who came between them.

The second covenant is the first, and it was repeated for the sake of its description. *Ghilaz* (firmness/heaviness) is a property of bodies, and it is used figuratively for meaning, exaggerating its sanctity, its greatness, and the weight of its excessive burden. It has been said: the solemn covenant is an oath by Allah to fulfil what was entrusted to them. The *lam* in ﴿so that He may ask﴾: it has been said it may be the *lam al-sayrura* (lam of ultimate outcome), meaning: He took the covenant from the prophets so that the matter would end up at such and such. The apparent meaning is that it is the *lam kay* (lam of purpose), meaning: We sent the messengers and took from them the covenants to convey, so that Allah would make His creation into two groups: a group He would question about their truthfulness, for the sake of establishing proof, and they would answer that they were truthful toward Allah in their faith and all their actions, so He would reward them for that; and a group that disbelieved, so the punishment prepared for them would befall them. The truthful ones in this view who are questioned are the believers. The pronoun in (their truthfulness) refers to them, and the object of (their truthfulness) is omitted, its estimated sense being: "about their truthfulness to His covenant." Or (their truthfulness) carries the meaning of (their affirming), and its object is omitted, meaning: "about their affirming the prophets," because whoever says to the truthful "you have spoken the truth," the truthful one is truthful in his statement. Or: "so that He may ask the prophets about what their nations answered them with," related by Ali ibn Isa. Or: "so that He may ask about fulfilling the covenant that He took from them," related by Ibn Shajarah. Or: "so that He may ask the prophets about their conveying the message to their peoples," said by Mujahid. In this there is an admonition (p-214), meaning: if the prophets are being questioned, then how about others? Mujahid also said: ﴿so that He may ask the truthful ones﴾ means those who conveyed from the messengers. End of quote. The questioning of the messengers is a rebuke to the disbelievers regarding them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?﴾ (Qur'an 5:116). And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ (Qur'an 7:6). (And He prepared) is conjoined to (We took), because the meaning is that Allah emphasized to the prophets the calling to His religion for the sake of rewarding the believers.

﴿And prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾. Or it is conjoined to what is indicated by ﴿so that He may ask the truthful﴾, as if He said: "So He rewarded the believers and prepared for the disbelievers." Both were said by al-Zamakhshari. It is permissible that in the first part something has been omitted, namely what the truthful were rewarded with, and they are the believers, while the reason was mentioned; and in the second part the reason has been omitted, while what they were punished with was mentioned. The estimated sense would be: "so that He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness, so He rewarded them; and that He may ask the disbelievers about what they answered their messengers with." This is like His saying: ﴿And the Day He calls to them and says, "What did you respond to the messengers?" Then the information will be obscured to them﴾ (Qur'an 28:65), and ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ (Qur'an 76:31). So what is mentioned in the first is omitted, while its counterpart is mentioned in the second, and what is mentioned in the second is omitted, while its counterpart is mentioned in the first. This is an eloquent method, and we have previously mentioned it in His saying: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who calls out﴾ (Qur'an 2:171), and we elaborated on it there.

**[Surah al-Ahzab (The Confederates)]**, seventy-three verses, Madani (revealed at Medina).

﴿In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

**[p. 207]** ﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿And rely upon God; and sufficient is God as Trustee.﴾ ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his chest. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar (the pre-Islamic practice of declaring one's wife unlawful like one's mother) your mothers. Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your claim by your mouths. But God says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then [they are] your brothers in religion and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God than the [other] believers and emigrants, except that you do to your allies a kindness. That is inscribed in the Book.﴾ ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant.﴾ ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when hosts came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And God is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9] ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about God [various] assumptions.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10] ﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11] ﴿And [mention] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "God and His Messenger promised us only delusion."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12] ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return," and a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed. They intended only to flee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13] ﴿And if they had been entered upon from all its sides, and then they had been asked to commit sedition, they would have given it, and they would not have delayed in it except briefly.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 14] ﴿And they had already covenanted with God before [this] that they would not turn their backs. And the covenant of God is ever questioned.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15] ﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little."﴾ ﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?" And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or any helper.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 16] ﴿God already knows those among you who hinder [others] and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not come to battle except briefly.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18] ﴿[They are] stingy toward you. But when fear comes, you see them looking to you, their eyes revolving like one who has fainted from death. But when the fear departs, they strike you with sharp tongues, stingy toward good. Those have not believed, so God has nullified their deeds. And that is ever easy for God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19] ﴿They think the confederates have not left; and if the confederates should come, they would wish to be among the desert Arabs asking about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 20] ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God often.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21] ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 22] ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits. And they have not altered [their commitment] at all.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23] ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 24] ﴿And God repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good. And God sufficed the believers in fighting. And God is ever Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25] ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took as captives. And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And God is ever over all things competent.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 26] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, "If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28] ﴿But if you desire God and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then indeed God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 29] ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold. And that is ever easy for God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30] ﴿And whoever of you is devoted to God and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 31] ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear God, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet; but speak with appropriate speech.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32] ﴿And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed, God is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34] ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard [theirs], and the men who remember God often and the women who remember [Him]: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35] ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36] ﴿And [mention] when you said to the one on whom God had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear God," while you concealed within yourself that which God would make manifest. And you feared the people, while God has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And the command of God is ever accomplished.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37] ﴿There is no difficulty upon the Prophet in what God has ordained for him. That is the way of God with those who passed on before. And the command of God is a decree decreed.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 38] ﴿[They are] those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and fear no one except God. And sufficient is God as Reckoner.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39] ﴿Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of God and the seal of the prophets. And God is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40] ﴿O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance and exalt Him morning and evening.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41] ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43] ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace." And He has prepared for them a noble reward. O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44] ﴿And as one who invites to God by His permission and as a light-giving lamp.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 46] ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is great bounty from God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47] ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon God. And sufficient is God as Trustee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48] ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no right to count any waiting period against them. So provide for them and release them in a graceful release.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49] ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose due dowries you have given, and those your right hand possesses from what God has returned to you as spoils, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this being] exclusively for you, not for the [other] believers. We already know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty upon you. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50] ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will. And there is no blame upon you if you seek [again] one whom you had set aside. That is more suitable that they should be content and not grieve, and that they should all be pleased with what you give them. And God knows what is in your hearts, and God is ever Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51] ﴿Women are not lawful for you after [this], nor to exchange them for [other] wives, even if their beauty should please you, except what your right hand possesses. And God is ever, over all things, Observant.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52] ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that would be an annoyance to the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you, but God is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to annoy the Messenger of God, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53] ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed God is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 54] ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or the sons of their brothers or the sons of their sisters or their women or those their right hands possess. And fear God; indeed, God is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 55] ﴿Indeed, God and His angels confer blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, confer blessings upon him and greet him with [complete] greeting.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56] ﴿Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger, God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57] ﴿And those who abuse believing men and believing women for what they have not earned have born the burden of slander and clear sin.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 58] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the wives of the believers that they should bring down over themselves some of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 59]

**[p. 208]** *Al-jawf* (the cavity, the inside of the body): a known thing, its plural is *ajwaf*.

*Yathrib*: the city of the Messenger, upon him peace. It is said: it is the land of Medina in one of its areas.

*Al-hanjara* (the top of the windpipe): the end of the *ghalsama* (the protruding part of the throat), and it is the terminus of the *hulqum* (the gullet); and the *hulqum* is the passage of food and drink.

*Al-aqtar*: the sides, singular *qutr*. It is also said *qutr* with a *ta'* (*qutr* / *qutr*), a dialectal variant of it.

*A'awwaqa 'an kadha*: he was held back from such and such, he was discouraged from it.

*Salaqahu*: he was bold against him and struck him. It is also said *salqahu* with a *sad*. The poet said:

*Fa-salaqna fi Murad salqatan wa-Sada' alhaqat-hum bi-al-thalal*
So we struck a blow among Murad, and among Sada' a blow that brought them to ruin.

It was also said: *salaqahu* means he addressed him with an eloquent address, and from it comes *khatib sallaq* and *mislaq* (a fluent orator), and *lisan sallaq* and *mislaq* (an eloquent tongue).

*Al-nahb*: the vow, and the thing that a person does not commit to but believes it is binding to fulfill. The poet said:

*'Ashiyyata farra al-Harithiyyuna ba'damā * * * qada nahbahu fi multaqa al-qawmi Hawbaru*
On the evening the Harithiyyun fled, after Hawbar had fulfilled his vow in the meeting-place of the people.

Jarir said:

*Bi-Tikhfata jalladna al-muluka wa-khaylunā * * * 'ashiyyata Bastamin jarayna 'ala nahbi*
At Tikhfa we fought the kings, and our horses ran on the evening of Bastam, upon a great matter.

That is: upon a great matter that one has committed himself to carry out. Death may also be called *nahb*.

*Al-sayasi*: the fortresses, singular *sayisa*, and it is everything by which one is protected. It is also said of the horn of the bull and the gazelle, and of the spur of the rooster, which is its claw in its leg, because it fortifies itself with it. *Al-sayasi* also means the shuttles of weavers, which are made of iron. From it is the saying of Durayd ibn al-Simma:

*Ka-wqi' al-sayasi fi al-nasiji al-mumaddadi*
Like the striking of the shuttles on the stretched woven cloth.

*Al-uswa*: the model, and its *hamza* may be pronounced with a *damma* or a *kasra*. One says *yatasa bi-Fulan*: he follows him as a model. *Al-uswa* is from *al-i'tisa'* (following as a model), as *al-qudwa* is from *al-iqtida'* (emulation): a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun.

*Al-tabarruj*: Al-Layth said: *tabarrajat* means she displayed her beauties of face and body, while it is still seen from her eye a good manner of looking. Abu 'Ubayda said: she brings out her beauties of that by which she arouses the desire of men. Its origin is from *barij*: in his eye and in his teeth there is *barij*, meaning spaciousness.

*Al-watar*: Abu 'Ubayda said: it is like *al-araba* (need, want). He recited for al-Rabi' ibn Asbagh:

**[p. 209]**

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 3)**

> "We bade farewell before he bade us farewell, when he had fulfilled his *wataran* (want) of our youth."

Al-Mubarrad said: *al-wataru* (*wataran*) is desire and love. It is said: "I have not fulfilled *wataran* from your meeting," meaning: "I have not enjoyed you until my soul desires [it]." He recited:

> "And how would my sojourning in Medina be, after Jamil ibn Ma'mar had fulfilled his *wataran* from it?"

*Al-jilbab*: a garment larger than the *khimar* (headscarf).

* *

﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed God is ever Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿And put your trust in God, and God suffices as a Guardian.﴾ ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by *zihar* your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying with your mouths. But God says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then [they are] your brothers in religion and your clients (*mawali*). And there is no blame upon you for what you have erred in, but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of relationship are closer to one another in the Book of God than [other] believers and emigrants, except that you do to your allies a kindness. That is written in the Book.﴾ ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant,﴾ ﴿that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.﴾

(p. 210) This surah is Medinan. It has been mentioned previously that his (ﷺ) being addressed as "O Prophet" (*ya ayyuha al-nabiyyu*), and in the verse, "O Messenger" (*ya ayyuha al-rasulu*) [al-Ma'idah 5:41], is by way of honour, esteem, and drawing attention to his station and excellence. Other prophets are addressed by their names, as in: ﴿O Adam﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:33], ﴿O Noah﴾ [Hud 11:32], ﴿O Abraham﴾ [Hud 11:76], ﴿O Moses﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:55], ﴿O David﴾ [Sad 38:26], ﴿O Jesus﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:55]. Where God mentions him in the form of information, that he is His messenger, He names him explicitly, saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ [al-Fath 48:29], ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:144], informing that he is His messenger and teaching them to call him by that. Where He does not intend to inform of that, his name comes as it does in the address: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:128], ﴿And the Messenger says, "My Lord..."﴾ [al-Furqan 25:30], ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers﴾, and other verses.

He commanded him to have *taqwa* (God-consciousness), though he was already characterised by it, meaning: to persist in it and increase in it. The apparent meaning is that this is a command to the Prophet (ﷺ); and if he is commanded in this, others are even more in need of this command. It has also been said that the address is to him in form, but its intended audience is his community (*ummah*).

It is related that when he came to Medina, and he loved the conversion of the Jews, some of them pledged allegiance to him while concealing hypocrisy. He was gentle towards them, and they displayed sincere advice while practising deception. Because of his alliance with them and his eagerness for their reconciliation, he would sometimes listen to them. So this was revealed as a warning to him against them and an alert to their enmity.

It is also related that Abu Sufyan, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami came during the truce that was between them and him. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and al-Jadd ibn Qays stood up and said to him: "Abandon mention of our gods and say that they intercede and benefit; and we will leave you and your Lord." This grieved him and the believers, and they intended to kill them, so this was revealed.

It was appropriate that He forbade him to obey the disbelievers, who openly display their disbelief, and the hypocrites, who display faith while concealing disbelief. The two causes encompass the two groups: that is, "do not obey the disbelievers of Mecca, nor the hypocrites of Medina, in what they request of you." It is related that the people of Mecca called him to return to their religion, and they would give him half their wealth and marry him to Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah's daughter; and the hypocrites of Medina frightened him that they would kill him if he did not return. So this was revealed.

The connection between the beginning of this surah and the end of what preceded it is clear: it had related that they were asking for the *fath* (decisive judgment), which is the separation between them; and God informed that on the Day of the *fath* their faith will not benefit them. So at the beginning of this surah He commanded him to fear God, and forbade him to obey the disbelievers and hypocrites in what they wished from him.

﴿Indeed God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of right from wrong, and of benefit from harm; All-Wise, who places things only in their proper places, governed by wisdom. Or: All-Knowing in that He commanded His *taqwa*, and that it should come from the depth of the heart; All-Wise in that He forbade obedience to the disbelievers and hypocrites. It has also been said that this is consolation for the Messenger, meaning: All-Knowing of who fears Him, All-Wise in guiding whom He wills and misguiding whom He wills.

Then He commanded him to follow what was revealed to him, which is the Qur'an, and to restrict himself to it, and to abandon the rites of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance).

Abu 'Amr read ﴿بِما يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ (*bima ya'malun*, "what they do"), in the first and second places, with the *ya* of the third person (absent); the rest of the seven read it with the *ta* of address (*bima ta'malun*). In the first place it could be an *iltifat* (shift of grammatical person), and it could also fit with His saying ﴿واتَّبِعْ﴾ (*wattabi'*, "and follow"). Then He commanded him (ﷺ) to entrust his affair to God. The discussion of ﴿كَفى بِاللَّهِ﴾ (*kafa billahi*, "God suffices") has already been given at the first place it occurs in the Qur'an.

It is related that there was a man among the Banu Fihr called Abu Ma'mar Jamil ibn Asad; it has also been said: Hamid ibn Ma'mar ibn Habib ibn Wahb ibn Harithah ibn Jumah. About him the poet says:

> "And how would my sojourning in Medina be, after Jamil ibn Ma'mar had fulfilled his *wataran* from it?"

He claimed that he had two hearts, and he was called *Dhu al-Qalbayn* (the Man of Two Hearts). He used to say: "I am more intelligent and understanding than Muhammad." When the news of the defeat at Badr reached him, his reason was disturbed, and he related to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb a tale like one who is deranged. So this was revealed.

Al-Hasan said: they were a group, each of whom would say: "A self commands me, and a self forbids me." It has also been said that some of the hypocrites said, "Muhammad has two hearts, because sometimes he is engaged in one matter, then he turns to another for a moment, then returns to his affair." So God negated that about him and about everyone.

It has been said: the way this verse is connected to what precedes it is that when God commanded *taqwa*, it was fitting that there should not be in the heart any *taqwa* other than God's. For a person does not have two hearts, by one of which he fears God and by the other something else. He fears something else only by turning the heart away from God towards another, and that is not fitting for one who fears God with true fear. End, summarised.

God has not made for a human two hearts, because either one of them does the same acts of the heart as the other, in which case there is no need for one of them; or it does something different, which leads to a person being described as desiring and hating, knowing and suspecting, doubting and being certain, in one state at the same time. The "body" (*jawf*) is mentioned, although it is known that the heart exists only within the body, for emphasis, for vividness, and to make the meaning clear, as He said: ﴿But it is the hearts within the breasts that become blind﴾ [al-Hajj 22:46]. So when he hears this, he imagines for himself a cavity containing two hearts, and hastens to deny it.

﴿Nor has He made your wives﴾: God did not make the wife whom one has declared *zihar* (a mother). For the mother is one who is served and to whom one lowers the wing of humility, while the wife is one who is employed and disposed of for bed and other purposes, like a slave; these are two opposing states.

Qalun and Qunbul read ﴿اللّائِي﴾ (*allai*, "those who") here, and in al-Mujadilah and al-Talaq, with *hamzah* and without *ya'*. Warsh read it with a *ya'* with a briefly-pronounced *kasrah* (*ya'* with a faint vowel). Al-Bazzi and Abu 'Amr read it with a quiescent *ya'* in place of the *hamzah*; this is a transmitted substitution, not a systematic one, and it is the dialect of Quraysh. The rest of the seven read it with *hamz* followed by *ya'*.

'Asim read ﴿تُظاهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzahiruna*, "you declare *zihar*") with *ta'* for address, and in al-Mujadilah with *ya'* for the third person, as the present tense of *zahara*. With doubled *zay* and *ha'*: the two Haramis (Meccan and Medinan readers) and Abu 'Amr; with doubled *zay* and an *alif* after it: Ibn 'Amir; with a single *zay* and *alif*: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i. Ibn 'Amir agreed with the others in al-Mujadilah. The rest of the seven read it with doubled *zay* there.

Ibn Wathtab read, as transmitted by Ibn 'Atiyyah, *yuzhiru* with *ya'* vowelled with *damma*, *zay* quiescent, and *ha'* with *kasra*, the present tense of *azhara*. As related by Abu Bakr al-Razi from him, with a single *zay*, the *ta'* of reflexive being omitted and *ha'* doubled. Al-Hasan read ﴿تُظْهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzhiruna*, Q. 30:18) with *ta'* vowelled with *damma*, single *zay*, and doubled *ha'*, the present tense of *zahhara* (with doubled *ha'*). Harun, from Abu 'Amr, read ﴿تُظْهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzhiruna*, Q. 30:18) with *ta'* and *ha'* vowelled with *fatha*, *zay* quiescent, the present tense of *zahara* with single *ha'*. In the codex of Ubayy: *tatazahharuna*, with two *ta's*.

These are nine readings. The meaning: he said to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother." These verbs are derived from this expression, like *labba* (the *muhrim* said *labbayka*, "here I am"), and *uffa* (when he said *uff*, "ugh"). The verb is construed with *min* (from), because *zihar* used to be a divorce in the Jahiliyyah, so they would avoid the wife who had been declared *zihar*, as they would avoid a divorced woman. The meaning is that he kept away from her by way of *zihar* and other means, that is, from his wife. Since the sense of distancing was implied, it is construed with *min*. They used the back as a euphemism for the belly, to keep away what is close to the private parts; and because they used to say that intercourse with a woman with her back to the sky is forbidden, while the people of Medina used to say that a child born in that position would be cross-eyed. They exaggerated in intensifying the prohibition of the wife, so He likened her to the back, then He went further and made her like the back of his mother.

It is related that Zayd ibn Harithah, of the Kalb, was captured as a child. Hakim ibn Hizam bought him for his aunt Khadijah, and she gave him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). His father and uncle came with the ransom for him, and that was before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent. He freed him, and they used to say: "Zayd ibn Muhammad." So this was revealed.

﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons (*ad'iya'akum*) your sons﴾: the verse. In the Jahiliyyah and the early period of Islam, when a man adopted another's son, he would inherit from him.

*Ad'iya'*: the plural of *da'iyy*, a form *fa'il* in the sense of *maf'ul* (passive: "one who is called"), which came irregularly. Its regular plural would be *fa'la* (like *jarih*, *jarha*). This plural is in fact the regular plural of the *fa'il* form with a weak final radical in the sense of *fa'il* (active), as in *taqiyy* and *atqiya'*. They made *ad'iya'* analogous to *taqiyy*, so they formed its plural irregularly, as they irregularly formed the plurals of *asir* and *qatil*, saying *usara'* and *qutala'*; though the regular forms of these two have also been heard, *asra* and *qatla*.

Sonship (*bunuwwah*) entails genuine descent in lineage, while adoption (*da'wah*) is attaching an accidental relationship by naming. So it cannot be that one thing is both genuine and not genuine. ﴿That﴾ (*dhalikum*): that is, their calling them sons is merely a statement, with no reality to its meaning, since the word does not correspond to the belief, for it is known in reality that he is not his son.

﴿And God says the truth﴾: that is, what agrees with the outward and the inward.

﴿And He guides to the way﴾: that is, the way of truth, which is His saying, ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾; or the way of the Law and faith.

The majority read ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ (*yahdi*) as the present tense of *hada*. Qatadah read it with *ya'* vowelled with *damma*, *ha'* with *fatha*, and doubled *dal*.

﴿Aqsatu﴾ (*aqsatu*, "more just") is the elative form, and its discussion has already been given at the end of al-Baqarah. Its meaning is "more equitable." When He commanded that the adopted son be called by his father's name if it is known, they said: "Zayd ibn Harithah" and ﴿your clients (*mawali-kum*)﴾; and for this reason they said: "Salim, client of Abu Hudhayfah." Al-Tabari mentioned that Abu Bakrah recited this verse and then said: "I am one of those whose father is not known, so I am your brother in religion and your client." Al-Razi said: "By God, if he knew his father was a donkey, he would have claimed kinship with him." The narrators of hadith say about him: Nufay' ibn al-Harith. And in a hadith: "Whoever claims a father other than his own, knowingly, God has forbidden him Paradise."

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verses 1–8 (part 3 of 3):

﴿In what you have erred in﴾. It has been said: He lifts the blame from them regarding what occurred before the prohibition. But this is weak, since what came before the prohibition cannot be described as an error. It has also been said: it refers to what the tongue slipped into. This is either by way of a slip, if that word occurred to them before the prohibition and passed over their tongues by mistake, or by way of tenderness and compassion, as a person often says to a young child "my son" just as he says to an elder "my father," as a form of honour and respect. The word *ma* (what) is conjoined to *ma akhta'tum* (what you erred in), meaning: "but the sin lies in what your hearts have intended." It has been permitted that *ma* be in the nominative position as the subject of a nominal sentence, meaning: "but what your hearts have intended is the sin." (And Allah is Forgiving) to the one who intends it if he repents, (Merciful) in that He lifts the blame from the one who errs.

As for his being, peace be upon him, ﴿closer to the believers than they are to themselves﴾, this means he is more compassionate toward them and more tender to them, since he calls them to salvation while their own selves call them to destruction. From this is his saying, peace be upon him: "I am holding you back by your waistbands from the Fire, while you are hurling yourselves into it like moths." And from the fact that he stands for them in the position of a father. Likewise in the codex of Ubayy and the recitation of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): "His wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them," meaning in religion. Mujahid said: every prophet is the father of his community. It has been said regarding the words of Lut, peace be upon him: "These are my daughters" (Qur'an 11:78), that he meant the believing women, i.e., his daughters in religion. Therefore it came: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ (Qur'an 49:10), i.e., in religion. And from him, peace be upon him: "There is no believer except that I am closer to him in this world and the Hereafter." And recite, if you wish: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves﴾. "Whichever believer dies leaving wealth, let his agnatic heirs ('asabah) inherit it, whoever they are; and if he leaves debt or dependents, then it is for me." It has been said: in His saying, the Exalted, ﴿closer to the believers﴾, the qualification is unrestricted, i.e., in every matter, and it was not limited. Therefore it is necessary that he be more beloved to them than their own selves, his judgment be more binding upon them than their own judgment, and his rights be given precedence, and other such matters that are obligatory for them regarding his right. End of quote. If this meaning were intended, the construction would have been: "The believers are closer to the Prophet than they are to themselves."

﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾, i.e., like their mothers in reverence and honour. And in some rulings, such as the prohibition of marrying them and other matters in which they are treated as strangers. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿and his wives﴾ is that it covers everyone who is described as being his wife, peace be upon him, whether he divorced her or did not divorce her. It has been said: this ruling does not apply to a divorced woman. It has also been said: whoever he consummated the marriage with, her prohibition is established with certainty. Umar intended to stone a woman whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had separated from, and who had married again afterward. She said to him: "Why this? He did not place a veil upon me, nor was I named a mother to the Muslims." So he refrained from her. At first in Medina there was inheritance by the brotherhood of Islam and by emigration, then Allah, the Exalted, ruled that blood relatives (ulu al-arham) have a better claim to inheritance than the brother in Islam, or by emigration, in the Book of Allah, i.e., in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), or in the Qur'an, of (p-213) the believers and the emigrants. That is, they are closer than the believers, who used to inherit merely by faith, and than the emigrants, who used to inherit by emigration. This is the apparent meaning, so the *min* (from) here is like the *min* in: "Zayd is better than Amr." Al-Zamakhshari said: it is permissible that it be an explanation of "blood relatives," meaning: the relatives, some of whom are closer than others to inherit from one another than strangers. End of quote. The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿to your allies﴾ is general, so it includes all its categories, whether relative or stranger, believer or disbeliever, to whom one shows kindness and whom one joins in life, and to whom one bequeaths at death. This was said by Qatadah, al-Hasan, Ata', and Ibn al-Hanafiyyah. Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, al-Rummani and others said: ﴿to your allies﴾ is specific to the believers.

The context of what preceded concerning the believers supports this. However, the bond of kinship is not removed from the disbeliever; what is removed is that one should cast affection toward him, like a guardian of Islam. This exception in His saying ﴿except that you do﴾ is something understood from the speech, meaning: ﴿blood relatives are closer to one another﴾ in benefit by inheritance and other things. It is transitive with *ila* (to) because the meaning is: "except that you give to your allies," which is an allusion to what is in the two verses. (In the Book) is either the Preserved Tablet or the Qur'an, as previously mentioned.

﴿Written﴾, i.e., inscribed in writing. This sentence is a new independent clause, like a conclusion to what has been mentioned of rulings. Since what preceded were rulings from Allah, the Exalted, and among them were matters from the pre-Islamic period and matters in Islam that were abrogated (naskh), He followed it with His saying: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾, i.e., to convey the laws and to call to Allah. So you are not an innovator in conveying from Allah. The governing element of *idh* (when), as stated by al-Hawfi and Ibn Atiyyah, may be (written), i.e., written in the Mother of the Book, and at the time when We took. It has been said: the governing element is "remember when We took." This covenant concerns conveying the messages of Allah and calling to faith, and no obstacle prevents them from it, neither fear nor desire. Al-Kalbi said: their covenant was taken to convey. Qatadah said: it was to confirm one another's truthfulness, to announce that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and for the Messenger of Allah to announce that there is no prophet after him. Al-Zajjaj and others said: what was taken from them was at the time of the extraction of the offspring of Adam from his loins like particles. They said: then Allah took at that time the covenant of the prophets to convey and to confirm one another, and to all that prophethood encompasses. Something similar was narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. These five were singled out for mention after being included among the prophets. It has been said: they are the Ulu al-'Azm (the prophets of firm resolve), due to their nobility and excellence over others. Muhammad was placed first because he is more excellent than them and has more followers. Noah was placed first in the verse of al-Shura, in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ (Qur'an 42:13), because its presentation there is different. There, it was presented as a description of the religion of Islam as the original religion, as if He said: He has legislated for you the original religion with which Noah was sent in the old covenant, with which Muhammad was sent, seal of the prophets, in the new covenant, and with which were sent the well-known prophets who came between them.

The second covenant is the first, and it was repeated for the sake of its description. *Ghilaz* (firmness/heaviness) is a property of bodies, and it is used figuratively for meaning, exaggerating its sanctity, its greatness, and the weight of its excessive burden. It has been said: the solemn covenant is an oath by Allah to fulfil what was entrusted to them. The *lam* in ﴿so that He may ask﴾: it has been said it may be the *lam al-sayrura* (lam of ultimate outcome), meaning: He took the covenant from the prophets so that the matter would end up at such and such. The apparent meaning is that it is the *lam kay* (lam of purpose), meaning: We sent the messengers and took from them the covenants to convey, so that Allah would make His creation into two groups: a group He would question about their truthfulness, for the sake of establishing proof, and they would answer that they were truthful toward Allah in their faith and all their actions, so He would reward them for that; and a group that disbelieved, so the punishment prepared for them would befall them. The truthful ones in this view who are questioned are the believers. The pronoun in (their truthfulness) refers to them, and the object of (their truthfulness) is omitted, its estimated sense being: "about their truthfulness to His covenant." Or (their truthfulness) carries the meaning of (their affirming), and its object is omitted, meaning: "about their affirming the prophets," because whoever says to the truthful "you have spoken the truth," the truthful one is truthful in his statement. Or: "so that He may ask the prophets about what their nations answered them with," related by Ali ibn Isa. Or: "so that He may ask about fulfilling the covenant that He took from them," related by Ibn Shajarah. Or: "so that He may ask the prophets about their conveying the message to their peoples," said by Mujahid. In this there is an admonition (p-214), meaning: if the prophets are being questioned, then how about others? Mujahid also said: ﴿so that He may ask the truthful ones﴾ means those who conveyed from the messengers. End of quote. The questioning of the messengers is a rebuke to the disbelievers regarding them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?﴾ (Qur'an 5:116). And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ (Qur'an 7:6). (And He prepared) is conjoined to (We took), because the meaning is that Allah emphasized to the prophets the calling to His religion for the sake of rewarding the believers.

﴿And prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾. Or it is conjoined to what is indicated by ﴿so that He may ask the truthful﴾, as if He said: "So He rewarded the believers and prepared for the disbelievers." Both were said by al-Zamakhshari. It is permissible that in the first part something has been omitted, namely what the truthful were rewarded with, and they are the believers, while the reason was mentioned; and in the second part the reason has been omitted, while what they were punished with was mentioned. The estimated sense would be: "so that He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness, so He rewarded them; and that He may ask the disbelievers about what they answered their messengers with." This is like His saying: ﴿And the Day He calls to them and says, "What did you respond to the messengers?" Then the information will be obscured to them﴾ (Qur'an 28:65), and ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ (Qur'an 76:31). So what is mentioned in the first is omitted, while its counterpart is mentioned in the second, and what is mentioned in the second is omitted, while its counterpart is mentioned in the first. This is an eloquent method, and we have previously mentioned it in His saying: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who calls out﴾ (Qur'an 2:171), and we elaborated on it there.

**[Surah al-Ahzab (The Confederates)]**, seventy-three verses, Madani (revealed at Medina).

﴿In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

**[p. 207]** ﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿And rely upon God; and sufficient is God as Trustee.﴾ ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his chest. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar (the pre-Islamic practice of declaring one's wife unlawful like one's mother) your mothers. Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your claim by your mouths. But God says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then [they are] your brothers in religion and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God than the [other] believers and emigrants, except that you do to your allies a kindness. That is inscribed in the Book.﴾ ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant.﴾ ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when hosts came to you, and We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And God is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 9] ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about God [various] assumptions.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10] ﴿There the believers were tested, and they were shaken with a severe shaking.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11] ﴿And [mention] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "God and His Messenger promised us only delusion."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12] ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return," and a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed. They intended only to flee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13] ﴿And if they had been entered upon from all its sides, and then they had been asked to commit sedition, they would have given it, and they would not have delayed in it except briefly.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 14] ﴿And they had already covenanted with God before [this] that they would not turn their backs. And the covenant of God is ever questioned.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 15] ﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little."﴾ ﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?" And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or any helper.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 16] ﴿God already knows those among you who hinder [others] and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us," and they do not come to battle except briefly.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18] ﴿[They are] stingy toward you. But when fear comes, you see them looking to you, their eyes revolving like one who has fainted from death. But when the fear departs, they strike you with sharp tongues, stingy toward good. Those have not believed, so God has nullified their deeds. And that is ever easy for God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19] ﴿They think the confederates have not left; and if the confederates should come, they would wish to be among the desert Arabs asking about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 20] ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God often.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21] ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 22] ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits. And they have not altered [their commitment] at all.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23] ﴿That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 24] ﴿And God repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good. And God sufficed the believers in fighting. And God is ever Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25] ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took as captives. And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And God is ever over all things competent.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 26] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, "If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28] ﴿But if you desire God and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then indeed God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 29] ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold. And that is ever easy for God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30] ﴿And whoever of you is devoted to God and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 31] ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear God, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet; but speak with appropriate speech.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32] ﴿And remain in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed, God is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34] ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humbly submissive men and humbly submissive women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard [theirs], and the men who remember God often and the women who remember [Him]: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35] ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36] ﴿And [mention] when you said to the one on whom God had bestowed favor and you had bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear God," while you concealed within yourself that which God would make manifest. And you feared the people, while God has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And the command of God is ever accomplished.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37] ﴿There is no difficulty upon the Prophet in what God has ordained for him. That is the way of God with those who passed on before. And the command of God is a decree decreed.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 38] ﴿[They are] those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and fear no one except God. And sufficient is God as Reckoner.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39] ﴿Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of God and the seal of the prophets. And God is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40] ﴿O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance and exalt Him morning and evening.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41] ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43] ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace." And He has prepared for them a noble reward. O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44] ﴿And as one who invites to God by His permission and as a light-giving lamp.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 46] ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is great bounty from God.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 47] ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon God. And sufficient is God as Trustee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48] ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no right to count any waiting period against them. So provide for them and release them in a graceful release.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49] ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose due dowries you have given, and those your right hand possesses from what God has returned to you as spoils, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this being] exclusively for you, not for the [other] believers. We already know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty upon you. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50] ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will. And there is no blame upon you if you seek [again] one whom you had set aside. That is more suitable that they should be content and not grieve, and that they should all be pleased with what you give them. And God knows what is in your hearts, and God is ever Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51] ﴿Women are not lawful for you after [this], nor to exchange them for [other] wives, even if their beauty should please you, except what your right hand possesses. And God is ever, over all things, Observant.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52] ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that would be an annoyance to the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you, but God is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to annoy the Messenger of God, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53] ﴿Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed God is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 54] ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or the sons of their brothers or the sons of their sisters or their women or those their right hands possess. And fear God; indeed, God is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 55] ﴿Indeed, God and His angels confer blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, confer blessings upon him and greet him with [complete] greeting.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56] ﴿Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger, God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57] ﴿And those who abuse believing men and believing women for what they have not earned have born the burden of slander and clear sin.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 58] ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the wives of the believers that they should bring down over themselves some of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 59]

**[p. 208]** *Al-jawf* (the cavity, the inside of the body): a known thing, its plural is *ajwaf*.

*Yathrib*: the city of the Messenger, upon him peace. It is said: it is the land of Medina in one of its areas.

*Al-hanjara* (the top of the windpipe): the end of the *ghalsama* (the protruding part of the throat), and it is the terminus of the *hulqum* (the gullet); and the *hulqum* is the passage of food and drink.

*Al-aqtar*: the sides, singular *qutr*. It is also said *qutr* with a *ta'* (*qutr* / *qutr*), a dialectal variant of it.

*A'awwaqa 'an kadha*: he was held back from such and such, he was discouraged from it.

*Salaqahu*: he was bold against him and struck him. It is also said *salqahu* with a *sad*. The poet said:

*Fa-salaqna fi Murad salqatan wa-Sada' alhaqat-hum bi-al-thalal*
So we struck a blow among Murad, and among Sada' a blow that brought them to ruin.

It was also said: *salaqahu* means he addressed him with an eloquent address, and from it comes *khatib sallaq* and *mislaq* (a fluent orator), and *lisan sallaq* and *mislaq* (an eloquent tongue).

*Al-nahb*: the vow, and the thing that a person does not commit to but believes it is binding to fulfill. The poet said:

*'Ashiyyata farra al-Harithiyyuna ba'damā * * * qada nahbahu fi multaqa al-qawmi Hawbaru*
On the evening the Harithiyyun fled, after Hawbar had fulfilled his vow in the meeting-place of the people.

Jarir said:

*Bi-Tikhfata jalladna al-muluka wa-khaylunā * * * 'ashiyyata Bastamin jarayna 'ala nahbi*
At Tikhfa we fought the kings, and our horses ran on the evening of Bastam, upon a great matter.

That is: upon a great matter that one has committed himself to carry out. Death may also be called *nahb*.

*Al-sayasi*: the fortresses, singular *sayisa*, and it is everything by which one is protected. It is also said of the horn of the bull and the gazelle, and of the spur of the rooster, which is its claw in its leg, because it fortifies itself with it. *Al-sayasi* also means the shuttles of weavers, which are made of iron. From it is the saying of Durayd ibn al-Simma:

*Ka-wqi' al-sayasi fi al-nasiji al-mumaddadi*
Like the striking of the shuttles on the stretched woven cloth.

*Al-uswa*: the model, and its *hamza* may be pronounced with a *damma* or a *kasra*. One says *yatasa bi-Fulan*: he follows him as a model. *Al-uswa* is from *al-i'tisa'* (following as a model), as *al-qudwa* is from *al-iqtida'* (emulation): a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun.

*Al-tabarruj*: Al-Layth said: *tabarrajat* means she displayed her beauties of face and body, while it is still seen from her eye a good manner of looking. Abu 'Ubayda said: she brings out her beauties of that by which she arouses the desire of men. Its origin is from *barij*: in his eye and in his teeth there is *barij*, meaning spaciousness.

*Al-watar*: Abu 'Ubayda said: it is like *al-araba* (need, want). He recited for al-Rabi' ibn Asbagh:

**[p. 209]**

**Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verses 1–8 (part 2 of 3)**

> "We bade farewell before he bade us farewell, when he had fulfilled his *wataran* (want) of our youth."

Al-Mubarrad said: *al-wataru* (*wataran*) is desire and love. It is said: "I have not fulfilled *wataran* from your meeting," meaning: "I have not enjoyed you until my soul desires [it]." He recited:

> "And how would my sojourning in Medina be, after Jamil ibn Ma'mar had fulfilled his *wataran* from it?"

*Al-jilbab*: a garment larger than the *khimar* (headscarf).

* *

﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed God is ever Aware of what you do.﴾ ﴿And put your trust in God, and God suffices as a Guardian.﴾ ﴿God has not made for any man two hearts within his body. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by *zihar* your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying with your mouths. But God says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾ ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then [they are] your brothers in religion and your clients (*mawali*). And there is no blame upon you for what you have erred in, but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts intended. And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of relationship are closer to one another in the Book of God than [other] believers and emigrants, except that you do to your allies a kindness. That is written in the Book.﴾ ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant,﴾ ﴿that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.﴾

(p. 210) This surah is Medinan. It has been mentioned previously that his (ﷺ) being addressed as "O Prophet" (*ya ayyuha al-nabiyyu*), and in the verse, "O Messenger" (*ya ayyuha al-rasulu*) [al-Ma'idah 5:41], is by way of honour, esteem, and drawing attention to his station and excellence. Other prophets are addressed by their names, as in: ﴿O Adam﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:33], ﴿O Noah﴾ [Hud 11:32], ﴿O Abraham﴾ [Hud 11:76], ﴿O Moses﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:55], ﴿O David﴾ [Sad 38:26], ﴿O Jesus﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:55]. Where God mentions him in the form of information, that he is His messenger, He names him explicitly, saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ [al-Fath 48:29], ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:144], informing that he is His messenger and teaching them to call him by that. Where He does not intend to inform of that, his name comes as it does in the address: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:128], ﴿And the Messenger says, "My Lord..."﴾ [al-Furqan 25:30], ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers﴾, and other verses.

He commanded him to have *taqwa* (God-consciousness), though he was already characterised by it, meaning: to persist in it and increase in it. The apparent meaning is that this is a command to the Prophet (ﷺ); and if he is commanded in this, others are even more in need of this command. It has also been said that the address is to him in form, but its intended audience is his community (*ummah*).

It is related that when he came to Medina, and he loved the conversion of the Jews, some of them pledged allegiance to him while concealing hypocrisy. He was gentle towards them, and they displayed sincere advice while practising deception. Because of his alliance with them and his eagerness for their reconciliation, he would sometimes listen to them. So this was revealed as a warning to him against them and an alert to their enmity.

It is also related that Abu Sufyan, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami came during the truce that was between them and him. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and al-Jadd ibn Qays stood up and said to him: "Abandon mention of our gods and say that they intercede and benefit; and we will leave you and your Lord." This grieved him and the believers, and they intended to kill them, so this was revealed.

It was appropriate that He forbade him to obey the disbelievers, who openly display their disbelief, and the hypocrites, who display faith while concealing disbelief. The two causes encompass the two groups: that is, "do not obey the disbelievers of Mecca, nor the hypocrites of Medina, in what they request of you." It is related that the people of Mecca called him to return to their religion, and they would give him half their wealth and marry him to Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah's daughter; and the hypocrites of Medina frightened him that they would kill him if he did not return. So this was revealed.

The connection between the beginning of this surah and the end of what preceded it is clear: it had related that they were asking for the *fath* (decisive judgment), which is the separation between them; and God informed that on the Day of the *fath* their faith will not benefit them. So at the beginning of this surah He commanded him to fear God, and forbade him to obey the disbelievers and hypocrites in what they wished from him.

﴿Indeed God is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of right from wrong, and of benefit from harm; All-Wise, who places things only in their proper places, governed by wisdom. Or: All-Knowing in that He commanded His *taqwa*, and that it should come from the depth of the heart; All-Wise in that He forbade obedience to the disbelievers and hypocrites. It has also been said that this is consolation for the Messenger, meaning: All-Knowing of who fears Him, All-Wise in guiding whom He wills and misguiding whom He wills.

Then He commanded him to follow what was revealed to him, which is the Qur'an, and to restrict himself to it, and to abandon the rites of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance).

Abu 'Amr read ﴿بِما يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ (*bima ya'malun*, "what they do"), in the first and second places, with the *ya* of the third person (absent); the rest of the seven read it with the *ta* of address (*bima ta'malun*). In the first place it could be an *iltifat* (shift of grammatical person), and it could also fit with His saying ﴿واتَّبِعْ﴾ (*wattabi'*, "and follow"). Then He commanded him (ﷺ) to entrust his affair to God. The discussion of ﴿كَفى بِاللَّهِ﴾ (*kafa billahi*, "God suffices") has already been given at the first place it occurs in the Qur'an.

It is related that there was a man among the Banu Fihr called Abu Ma'mar Jamil ibn Asad; it has also been said: Hamid ibn Ma'mar ibn Habib ibn Wahb ibn Harithah ibn Jumah. About him the poet says:

> "And how would my sojourning in Medina be, after Jamil ibn Ma'mar had fulfilled his *wataran* from it?"

He claimed that he had two hearts, and he was called *Dhu al-Qalbayn* (the Man of Two Hearts). He used to say: "I am more intelligent and understanding than Muhammad." When the news of the defeat at Badr reached him, his reason was disturbed, and he related to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb a tale like one who is deranged. So this was revealed.

Al-Hasan said: they were a group, each of whom would say: "A self commands me, and a self forbids me." It has also been said that some of the hypocrites said, "Muhammad has two hearts, because sometimes he is engaged in one matter, then he turns to another for a moment, then returns to his affair." So God negated that about him and about everyone.

It has been said: the way this verse is connected to what precedes it is that when God commanded *taqwa*, it was fitting that there should not be in the heart any *taqwa* other than God's. For a person does not have two hearts, by one of which he fears God and by the other something else. He fears something else only by turning the heart away from God towards another, and that is not fitting for one who fears God with true fear. End, summarised.

God has not made for a human two hearts, because either one of them does the same acts of the heart as the other, in which case there is no need for one of them; or it does something different, which leads to a person being described as desiring and hating, knowing and suspecting, doubting and being certain, in one state at the same time. The "body" (*jawf*) is mentioned, although it is known that the heart exists only within the body, for emphasis, for vividness, and to make the meaning clear, as He said: ﴿But it is the hearts within the breasts that become blind﴾ [al-Hajj 22:46]. So when he hears this, he imagines for himself a cavity containing two hearts, and hastens to deny it.

﴿Nor has He made your wives﴾: God did not make the wife whom one has declared *zihar* (a mother). For the mother is one who is served and to whom one lowers the wing of humility, while the wife is one who is employed and disposed of for bed and other purposes, like a slave; these are two opposing states.

Qalun and Qunbul read ﴿اللّائِي﴾ (*allai*, "those who") here, and in al-Mujadilah and al-Talaq, with *hamzah* and without *ya'*. Warsh read it with a *ya'* with a briefly-pronounced *kasrah* (*ya'* with a faint vowel). Al-Bazzi and Abu 'Amr read it with a quiescent *ya'* in place of the *hamzah*; this is a transmitted substitution, not a systematic one, and it is the dialect of Quraysh. The rest of the seven read it with *hamz* followed by *ya'*.

'Asim read ﴿تُظاهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzahiruna*, "you declare *zihar*") with *ta'* for address, and in al-Mujadilah with *ya'* for the third person, as the present tense of *zahara*. With doubled *zay* and *ha'*: the two Haramis (Meccan and Medinan readers) and Abu 'Amr; with doubled *zay* and an *alif* after it: Ibn 'Amir; with a single *zay* and *alif*: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i. Ibn 'Amir agreed with the others in al-Mujadilah. The rest of the seven read it with doubled *zay* there.

Ibn Wathtab read, as transmitted by Ibn 'Atiyyah, *yuzhiru* with *ya'* vowelled with *damma*, *zay* quiescent, and *ha'* with *kasra*, the present tense of *azhara*. As related by Abu Bakr al-Razi from him, with a single *zay*, the *ta'* of reflexive being omitted and *ha'* doubled. Al-Hasan read ﴿تُظْهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzhiruna*, Q. 30:18) with *ta'* vowelled with *damma*, single *zay*, and doubled *ha'*, the present tense of *zahhara* (with doubled *ha'*). Harun, from Abu 'Amr, read ﴿تُظْهِرُونَ﴾ (*tuzhiruna*, Q. 30:18) with *ta'* and *ha'* vowelled with *fatha*, *zay* quiescent, the present tense of *zahara* with single *ha'*. In the codex of Ubayy: *tatazahharuna*, with two *ta's*.

These are nine readings. The meaning: he said to her, "You are to me like the back of my mother." These verbs are derived from this expression, like *labba* (the *muhrim* said *labbayka*, "here I am"), and *uffa* (when he said *uff*, "ugh"). The verb is construed with *min* (from), because *zihar* used to be a divorce in the Jahiliyyah, so they would avoid the wife who had been declared *zihar*, as they would avoid a divorced woman. The meaning is that he kept away from her by way of *zihar* and other means, that is, from his wife. Since the sense of distancing was implied, it is construed with *min*. They used the back as a euphemism for the belly, to keep away what is close to the private parts; and because they used to say that intercourse with a woman with her back to the sky is forbidden, while the people of Medina used to say that a child born in that position would be cross-eyed. They exaggerated in intensifying the prohibition of the wife, so He likened her to the back, then He went further and made her like the back of his mother.

It is related that Zayd ibn Harithah, of the Kalb, was captured as a child. Hakim ibn Hizam bought him for his aunt Khadijah, and she gave him to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). His father and uncle came with the ransom for him, and that was before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent. He freed him, and they used to say: "Zayd ibn Muhammad." So this was revealed.

﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons (*ad'iya'akum*) your sons﴾: the verse. In the Jahiliyyah and the early period of Islam, when a man adopted another's son, he would inherit from him.

*Ad'iya'*: the plural of *da'iyy*, a form *fa'il* in the sense of *maf'ul* (passive: "one who is called"), which came irregularly. Its regular plural would be *fa'la* (like *jarih*, *jarha*). This plural is in fact the regular plural of the *fa'il* form with a weak final radical in the sense of *fa'il* (active), as in *taqiyy* and *atqiya'*. They made *ad'iya'* analogous to *taqiyy*, so they formed its plural irregularly, as they irregularly formed the plurals of *asir* and *qatil*, saying *usara'* and *qutala'*; though the regular forms of these two have also been heard, *asra* and *qatla*.

Sonship (*bunuwwah*) entails genuine descent in lineage, while adoption (*da'wah*) is attaching an accidental relationship by naming. So it cannot be that one thing is both genuine and not genuine. ﴿That﴾ (*dhalikum*): that is, their calling them sons is merely a statement, with no reality to its meaning, since the word does not correspond to the belief, for it is known in reality that he is not his son.
