Martyred from among the Muslims in the Battle of the Trench were: Muʿadh, Anas ibn Aws ibn ʿAtik, ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl, and Abu ʿAmr, who were from the Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal; al-Tufayl ibn al-Nuʿman and Thaʿlabah ibn Ghanamah, who were from the Banu Salamah; and Kaʿb ibn Zayd, from the Banu Dhubyan ibn al-Najjar, who was struck by a stray arrow and killed. Quraysh did not attack the Muslims after the Trench, and Allah sufficed them against the continuation and recurrence of fighting by defeating them afterward, and that was by His strength and might. It is related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: "We were detained on the day of the Trench, so we did not pray the noon prayer, nor the afternoon prayer, nor the sunset prayer, nor the night prayer, until after a portion of the night had passed, when we were relieved. Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting⁠﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then commanded Bilal, who gave the call to prayer and performed the noon prayer excellently, then each prayer after that with an iqamah."

And He brought down those who supported them (﴿وأنْزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهُمْ﴾), meaning those who aided the Quraysh and those with them among the confederates (al-Ahzab) from the People of the Book. They were the Jews of Banu Qurayzah, as the majority (al-Jumhur) hold. It is related from al-Hasan that they were Banu al-Nadir. The casting of terror was the cause of their coming down, but He mentioned the effect first, because the joy at their coming down was greater and the report of it was more important, so it was given precedence.

A man said: "O Messenger of God, Dihyah al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a silk saddle-cloth on it." He said: "That was Gabriel, peace be upon him, who was sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts."

When the confederates returned, Gabriel came at the time of noon and said: "God commands you to go out to Banu Qurayzah." So he called out among the people: "None of you shall pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." They set out for it. Some prayed on the road, and saw that this was meant as emphasis and urgency. Others prayed after the night prayer (al-'Isha'), and each was correct.

He besieged them for twenty-five nights. It is also said twenty-one, and it is also said fifteen. Then they came down under the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Awsi, because of an alliance that had existed between them, and they hoped for his kindness toward them. He judged that the fighting men should be killed, and the children, women and property should be taken as captives, and that the land and its produce should belong to the emigrants (al-Muhajirun) to the exclusion of the Helpers (al-Ansar). The Helpers spoke to him about this, and he said: "I wanted them to have property as you have." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of God from above the seven heavens." Then he had them brought down, and dug a trench for them in the marketplace of Madinah, and brought them forward and struck off their necks. They were between eight hundred and nine hundred. It is also said that there were six hundred fighting men and seven hundred captives.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadiri was brought, the one who had led them into treachery against the Messenger of God. He had entered among them out of loyalty to them, so he was left among those who were left to the judgment of Sa'd. When he drew near, wearing two garments of pale-yellow (tuffahiyyatan) cloth, his hands tied to his neck, he saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, by God, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes God will be forsaken." Then he said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of God and His decree, and it is a trial that was prescribed for the Children of Israel." Then he went forward and his neck was struck.

Someone from Banu Tha'labah said about him:
"By your life, the son of Akhtab did not blame himself,
but whoever forsakes God will be forsaken.
He strove until he had made his soul's excuse plain,
and he shook loose every one who seeks glory and stirs up strife."

He also killed one of their women, who was Lubabah, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had dropped a millstone on Khallad ibn Suwayd, and he was killed. No one other than him was martyred during the siege of Banu Qurayzah. Abu Sufyan ibn Mihsan, the brother of 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, died during the siege. The conquest of Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the fifth year after the Hijrah.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read (﴿وتَأْسِرُونَ﴾) "and you take captive" with the second-person ta' and a kasrah on the sin. Abu Haywah read both with a dammah. Al-Yamani read with the third-person ya'. Ibn Anas, on the authority of Ibn Dhakwan, read with the third-person ya' in both ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ وتَأْسِرُونَ﴾ (some you kill and some you take captive).

﴿وأوْرَثَكُمْ﴾ (and made you inherit) indicates that this passed to them after the death of those who were killed and of those who were removed from their land. It was mentioned first because of the great benefit of it from palm-groves and crops, and because they took possession of it a second time, along with their property, so that it might be used to strengthen the Muslims for jihad. It is also because it was in their houses, so the taking of possession of it was a third time.

﴿وأرْضًا لَمْ تَطَئُوها﴾ (and land you had not trodden) is a true promise of the opening of lands, such as Iraq, Syria, Yemen, Makkah, and all the other conquests of the Muslims. 'Ikrimah said: God informed them that He had decreed this. Al-Hasan said: He meant Rome and Persia. Qatadah said: "We used to say that it is Makkah." Muqatil, Yazid ibn Ruman and Ibn Zayd said: it is Khaybar. It is also said: Yemen. There is no basis for these specifications, and among the strange interpretations is that He meant their women.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿تَطَئُوها﴾ with a damma on the hamzah followed by a waw. Zayd ibn 'Ali read "lam tatuwha" (لَمْ تَطُوها) without the hamzah, changing the hamzah of "tata'u" into an alif, following the line of poetry:
"Indeed the beasts of prey lie still in their lairs,
but people are never guarded against their evil at all."
So the sakin alif met the waw and was dropped, as in your saying: "lam taraw-ha" (لَمْ تَرَوْها).

God concluded this verse with His power over everything, so nothing can overcome Him. This contained an indication of His granting the Muslims many conquests, and that He does not consider this unlikely. Just as He gave them possession of these, so He is able to give them possession of other lands.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verses 21–27 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much.﴾ ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly." And it increased them only in faith and submission.﴾ ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is one who awaits, and they have not altered in the least.﴾ ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good. And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting, and Allah is ever Strong and Mighty.﴾ ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took captive.﴾ ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and a land you had not trodden. And Allah is ever over all things Competent.﴾

The apparent meaning is that the address in His words ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have﴾ is to the believers, due to His words before it: ﴿and even if they had been among you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 20], and His words after it: ﴿for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. The meaning is: for you in him (ﷺ) is the model to follow. Just as he helped you and supported you, to the point that he fought his enemy with his own self, so that his noble front tooth was broken, his noble face was wounded, his uncle was killed, and he was afflicted with various kinds of harm; it is incumbent upon you to help him and support him, and not to hold yourselves in preference to his self, nor to his place where he is, and to expend your selves in his defense. For what you gained of the guidance to Islam is greater than everything you do with him of support and jihad in the way of Allah. The view of whoever said it is an address to the hypocrites is far-fetched.

﴿And the Last Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. It was said: the Day of the Ṣiyāq (the moment of death). ﴿Uswah⁠﴾ is the subject of kāna, and (lakum) is the predicate. ﴿Fī Rasūl Allāh⁠﴾ is connected to what (lakum) is connected to, or it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), because if it were postponed it could be an adjective of (uswah). Or it is connected to (kāna), according to the view of those who permit the defective kāna and its sisters to govern the adverbial and prepositional phrase. It is also permissible that ﴿fī Rasūl Allāh⁠﴾ is the predicate, and (lakum) is an explanation, i.e., for you, namely: ﴿for whoever hopes in Allah⁠﴾. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it is a substitute (badal) for (lakum), like His saying: ﴿to those who were deemed weak, to whoever among them believed⁠﴾ [al-A‘raf: 75]. End of quotation. According to the view of the majority of the Basrans, it is not permissible to substitute a noun for a pronoun of the first or second person, in the substitution of a thing from a thing when they refer to one and the same entity; the Kufans and al-Akhfash permitted it, and the saying of the poet supports it:

"By you Quraysh we were sufficed against every difficulty, and whoever was astray was guided to the path of guidance."

The majority read ﴿iswah⁠﴾ with a kasra on the hamza; ʿĀṣim read it with a ḍamma. Al-rajā’ means hope or fear. He linked hope with the remembrance of Allah, and the one who follows the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who is hopeful and remembering. When Allah the Exalted explained the hypocrites and their saying: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion⁠﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12], He explained the state of the believers and their saying, the opposite of what the hypocrites said. Allah had promised them that He would shake them until they sought His help, in His saying: ﴿Or do you think you will enter Paradise⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], and so on. When the confederates came and they rose to fight, and they were agitated, they said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised⁠﴾, and they were certain of Paradise and victory.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "The confederates are marching toward you in nine or ten [days]," meaning: at the end of nine or ten nights. So when they saw them coming to the appointed encounter, they said that. It was also said: the promise is what came in the verse concerning what he (peace be upon him) was promised when he ordered the digging of the trench, for he informed them that they would be besieged, ordered them to prepare for it, and informed them that they would be given victory after that. When they saw (p-223) the confederates, they said that, so they submitted at the first of the matter and awaited its end. This is a reference to the calamity, faith in Allah and in what the Messenger (ﷺ) informed of that had not yet occurred, like your saying: the conquest of Mecca, Persia, and Byzantium. Thus the increase is in what is believed, not in faith itself.

Ibn Abi ʿAblah read ﴿wa-mā zādūhum⁠﴾ [Hud: 101] with a waw, and the plural pronoun refers to the confederates. You say: "I told Zayd the truth (ṣadaqtu Zaydan al-ḥadīth)" and "I told Zayd in the matter (fi al-ḥadīth)." This ṣadaqa has been counted among verbs that transitively take a prepositional particle, and its origin is that, then it is extended so the particle is dropped and the verb reaches its object directly. From this is their proverb: "ṣadaqanī sinn Bakrihi," meaning: "in the age of Bakr." As for ﴿mā ʿāhadū⁠﴾, either it is with the particle dropped, meaning "in what they pledged," with the first object omitted, the estimate being "they were true to Allah," or ṣadaqa is transitive to one object, as you say: "your brother was truthful with me" when he told you the truth, and "your brother lied to you" when he told you a lie. The thing pledged was metaphorically "told the truth," as if they said to the one they pledged to: "We will be faithful to you," and they fulfilled it, so they were truthful to him; had they broken it, they would have lied to him, and it would have been a lie.

These men — Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the seventy of the Aqabah, the people of the pledge. Anas said: it was revealed concerning a people who had not witnessed Badr, who pledged not to fall behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they fulfilled it. Zayd ibn Ruman said: the Banu Harithah.

﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow⁠﴾. This is a figurative usage, because death is a matter that must befall a person, so it is called a vow (naḥb) for that reason. Mujahid said: "qaḍā naḥbahu" means his covenant. Abu ʿUbaydah said: his vow. Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow⁠﴾ may mean his death as a martyr, and it may mean his fulfilling his vow of steadfastness with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Another group said: those described as having fulfilled their vow are a group of the Companions who fulfilled the covenants of Islam completely. So the martyrs are among them, and the ten who were testified by the Messenger (ﷺ) to Paradise, and among them are those who attained this rank by what was not specifically stated. This statement is confirmed by the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was asked: "Who is the one who has fulfilled his vow?" while he was on the pulpit, and Talhah ibn ʿUbaydullah entered, and he said: "This is one of those who has fulfilled his vow."

﴿And among them is one who awaits⁠﴾. If qaḍāʾ al-naḥb is interpreted as martyrdom, the estimate is: and among them is one who awaits martyrdom; if it is interpreted as fulfilling the covenants of Islam, the estimate is: and among them is one who awaits attaining the highest ranks of faith and righteousness. Mujahid said: he awaits a day in which there is jihad, so that he fulfills his vow.

﴿And they did not alter⁠﴾: neither the martyrs nor the one who awaits. Talhah stood firm on the day of Uhud until his hand was struck, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Talhah has made it obligatory (awjaba)." This contains an allusion to those hypocrites who altered when they turned their backs, though they had pledged not to turn their backs.

﴿That Allah may reward the truthful⁠﴾: that is, those who ﴿were true to what they pledged to Allah⁠﴾, ﴿for their truthfulness⁠﴾, that is, because of their truthfulness.

﴿And punish the hypocrites if He wills⁠﴾. Their punishment is certain, so how is its conditioning on will valid, since He has willed to punish them if they persist in hypocrisy? Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: the fruit of punishing the hypocrites is their persistence in hypocrisy until death, and repentance is parallel to that persistence, and the fruit of repentance is that they are left without punishment. So there are two degrees: persistence in hypocrisy, or repentance from it. And from these two come two fruits: punishment, or mercy. Thus He mentioned, by way of brevity, one of these two and one of these two, and what He mentioned indicates what was omitted. What shows that the meaning of His words ﴿to punish⁠﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73] is "that they may persist in hypocrisy" is His words "if He wills" and its counterpart with repentance, and the omission of "or." End of quotation. What was mentioned amounts to this: the estimate is: that they may persist in hypocrisy and die upon it; if He wills, He punishes them, or He turns to them in repentance and has mercy on them. So the cause of punishment is omitted and its effect is mentioned, which is punishment; and the cause of mercy and forgiveness is mentioned and its effect, which is mercy and forgiveness, is omitted. This is a fine brevity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: and He punishes them if He wills, if they do not repent, and He turns to them if they repent. End of quotation. It is not permissible to make the punishment of those who do not repent conditional upon His will, since He has willed that and has informed that He will punish the hypocrites definitively and without doubt. The lam in ﴿li-yajziya⁠﴾ is said to be the lam of consequence (lam al-ṣayrūrah); and it was said: the lam of causation, connected to His words ﴿and they did not alter any alteration⁠﴾. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the hypocrites are treated as though they intended the evil outcome and sought it by their alteration, just as the truthful intended the outcome of truthfulness by their fulfillment; for both groups are led toward an outcome of reward and punishment, so it is as though they were equal in seeking and striving to attain them. Al-Suddi said: the meaning is: if He wills, He causes them to die in their hypocrisy, or He turns to them by their act of abandoning hypocrisy through accepting faith. It was also said: He punishes them in this world if He wills, and turns to them if He wills.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾: that is, forgiving of the sin, merciful in accepting repentance.

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved⁠﴾: the confederates from Medina, and the believers back to their lands.

﴿In their rage⁠﴾: this is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the bāʾ indicates accompaniment; and ﴿they gained no good⁠﴾ is a second circumstantial clause, or it is from the pronoun in (bi-ghayẓihim), making it an interlocking circumstantial clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the second may be an explanation of the first, or a new sentence. End of quotation. It does not appear that it is an explanation of the first, nor a new sentence, because it would remain detached from what precedes it.

﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting⁠﴾: by sending the wind and the hosts, who were the angels, so there was no fighting between the believers and the disbelievers. It was also said: the intended ones are ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib and those with him, who came out for fighting and called to it. ʿAlī killed ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd (Wudd) from among the disbelievers in single combat, when ʿAmr sought single combat, and ʿAlī came out to him. ʿAmr said: "I do not wish to kill you because of my companionship with your father." ʿAlī said to him: "But I wish to kill you," and ʿAli killed him in single combat. Nawfal ibn al-Harith, of Quraysh, plunged into the trench with his horse and was killed there. Also killed from among the disbelievers were Munabbih ibn ʿUthman and ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbaq. Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting⁠﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then commanded Bilal, who gave the call to prayer and performed the noon prayer excellently, then each prayer after that with an iqamah."

The meaning is: for you in him (ﷺ) is the model to follow. Just as he helped you and supported you, to the point that he fought his enemy with his own self, so that his noble front tooth was broken, his noble face was wounded, his uncle was killed, and he was afflicted with various kinds of harm; it is incumbent upon you to help him and support him, and not to hold yourselves in preference to his self, nor to his place where he is, and to expend your selves in his defense. For what you gained of the guidance to Islam is greater than everything you do with him of support and jihad in the way of Allah. The view of whoever said it is an address to the hypocrites is far-fetched.

﴿And the Last Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. It was said: the Day of the Ṣiyāq (the moment of death). ﴿Uswah⁠﴾ is the subject of kāna, and (lakum) is the predicate. ﴿Fī Rasūl Allāh⁠﴾ is connected to what (lakum) is connected to, or it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), because if it were postponed it could be an adjective of (uswah). Or it is connected to (kāna), according to the view of those who permit the defective kāna and its sisters to govern the adverbial and prepositional phrase. It is also permissible that ﴿fī Rasūl Allāh⁠﴾ is the predicate, and (lakum) is an explanation, i.e., for you, namely: ﴿for whoever hopes in Allah⁠﴾. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it is a substitute (badal) for (lakum), like His saying: ﴿to those who were deemed weak, to whoever among them believed⁠﴾ [al-A‘raf: 75]. End of quotation. According to the view of the majority of the Basrans, it is not permissible to substitute a noun for a pronoun of the first or second person, in the substitution of a thing from a thing when they refer to one and the same entity; the Kufans and al-Akhfash permitted it, and the saying of the poet supports it:

"By you Quraysh we were sufficed against every difficulty, and whoever was astray was guided to the path of guidance."

The majority read ﴿iswah⁠﴾ with a kasra on the hamza; ʿĀṣim read it with a ḍamma. Al-rajā’ means hope or fear. He linked hope with the remembrance of Allah, and the one who follows the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who is hopeful and remembering. When Allah the Exalted explained the hypocrites and their saying: ﴿Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion⁠﴾ [al-Ahzab: 12], He explained the state of the believers and their saying, the opposite of what the hypocrites said. Allah had promised them that He would shake them until they sought His help, in His saying: ﴿Or do you think you will enter Paradise⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], and so on. When the confederates came and they rose to fight, and they were agitated, they said: ﴿This is what Allah and His Messenger promised⁠﴾, and they were certain of Paradise and victory.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "The confederates are marching toward you in nine or ten [days]," meaning: at the end of nine or ten nights. So when they saw them coming to the appointed encounter, they said that. It was also said: the promise is what came in the verse concerning what he (peace be upon him) was promised when he ordered the digging of the trench, for he informed them that they would be besieged, ordered them to prepare for it, and informed them that they would be given victory after that. When they saw (p-223) the confederates, they said that, so they submitted at the first of the matter and awaited its end. This is a reference to the calamity, faith in Allah and in what the Messenger (ﷺ) informed of that had not yet occurred, like your saying: the conquest of Mecca, Persia, and Byzantium. Thus the increase is in what is believed, not in faith itself.

Ibn Abi ʿAblah read ﴿wa-mā zādūhum⁠﴾ [Hud: 101] with a waw, and the plural pronoun refers to the confederates. You say: "I told Zayd the truth (ṣadaqtu Zaydan al-ḥadīth)" and "I told Zayd in the matter (fi al-ḥadīth)." This ṣadaqa has been counted among verbs that transitively take a prepositional particle, and its origin is that, then it is extended so the particle is dropped and the verb reaches its object directly. From this is their proverb: "ṣadaqanī sinn Bakrihi," meaning: "in the age of Bakr." As for ﴿mā ʿāhadū⁠﴾, either it is with the particle dropped, meaning "in what they pledged," with the first object omitted, the estimate being "they were true to Allah," or ṣadaqa is transitive to one object, as you say: "your brother was truthful with me" when he told you the truth, and "your brother lied to you" when he told you a lie. The thing pledged was metaphorically "told the truth," as if they said to the one they pledged to: "We will be faithful to you," and they fulfilled it, so they were truthful to him; had they broken it, they would have lied to him, and it would have been a lie.

These men — Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the seventy of the Aqabah, the people of the pledge. Anas said: it was revealed concerning a people who had not witnessed Badr, who pledged not to fall behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they fulfilled it. Zayd ibn Ruman said: the Banu Harithah.

﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow⁠﴾. This is a figurative usage, because death is a matter that must befall a person, so it is called a vow (naḥb) for that reason. Mujahid said: "qaḍā naḥbahu" means his covenant. Abu ʿUbaydah said: his vow. Al-Zamakhsharī said: ﴿So among them is one who has fulfilled his vow⁠﴾ may mean his death as a martyr, and it may mean his fulfilling his vow of steadfastness with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Another group said: those described as having fulfilled their vow are a group of the Companions who fulfilled the covenants of Islam completely. So the martyrs are among them, and the ten who were testified by the Messenger (ﷺ) to Paradise, and among them are those who attained this rank by what was not specifically stated. This statement is confirmed by the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was asked: "Who is the one who has fulfilled his vow?" while he was on the pulpit, and Talhah ibn ʿUbaydullah entered, and he said: "This is one of those who has fulfilled his vow."

﴿And among them is one who awaits⁠﴾. If qaḍāʾ al-naḥb is interpreted as martyrdom, the estimate is: and among them is one who awaits martyrdom; if it is interpreted as fulfilling the covenants of Islam, the estimate is: and among them is one who awaits attaining the highest ranks of faith and righteousness. Mujahid said: he awaits a day in which there is jihad, so that he fulfills his vow.

﴿And they did not alter⁠﴾: neither the martyrs nor the one who awaits. Talhah stood firm on the day of Uhud until his hand was struck, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Talhah has made it obligatory (awjaba)." This contains an allusion to those hypocrites who altered when they turned their backs, though they had pledged not to turn their backs.

﴿That Allah may reward the truthful⁠﴾: that is, those who ﴿were true to what they pledged to Allah⁠﴾, ﴿for their truthfulness⁠﴾, that is, because of their truthfulness.

﴿And punish the hypocrites if He wills⁠﴾. Their punishment is certain, so how is its conditioning on will valid, since He has willed to punish them if they persist in hypocrisy? Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: the fruit of punishing the hypocrites is their persistence in hypocrisy until death, and repentance is parallel to that persistence, and the fruit of repentance is that they are left without punishment. So there are two degrees: persistence in hypocrisy, or repentance from it. And from these two come two fruits: punishment, or mercy. Thus He mentioned, by way of brevity, one of these two and one of these two, and what He mentioned indicates what was omitted. What shows that the meaning of His words ﴿to punish⁠﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73] is "that they may persist in hypocrisy" is His words "if He wills" and its counterpart with repentance, and the omission of "or." End of quotation. What was mentioned amounts to this: the estimate is: that they may persist in hypocrisy and die upon it; if He wills, He punishes them, or He turns to them in repentance and has mercy on them. So the cause of punishment is omitted and its effect is mentioned, which is punishment; and the cause of mercy and forgiveness is mentioned and its effect, which is mercy and forgiveness, is omitted. This is a fine brevity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: and He punishes them if He wills, if they do not repent, and He turns to them if they repent. End of quotation. It is not permissible to make the punishment of those who do not repent conditional upon His will, since He has willed that and has informed that He will punish the hypocrites definitively and without doubt. The lam in ﴿li-yajziya⁠﴾ is said to be the lam of consequence (lam al-ṣayrūrah); and it was said: the lam of causation, connected to His words ﴿and they did not alter any alteration⁠﴾. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the hypocrites are treated as though they intended the evil outcome and sought it by their alteration, just as the truthful intended the outcome of truthfulness by their fulfillment; for both groups are led toward an outcome of reward and punishment, so it is as though they were equal in seeking and striving to attain them. Al-Suddi said: the meaning is: if He wills, He causes them to die in their hypocrisy, or He turns to them by their act of abandoning hypocrisy through accepting faith. It was also said: He punishes them in this world if He wills, and turns to them if He wills.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾: that is, forgiving of the sin, merciful in accepting repentance.

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved⁠﴾: the confederates from Medina, and the believers back to their lands.

﴿In their rage⁠﴾: this is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the bāʾ indicates accompaniment; and ﴿they gained no good⁠﴾ is a second circumstantial clause, or it is from the pronoun in (bi-ghayẓihim), making it an interlocking circumstantial clause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the second may be an explanation of the first, or a new sentence. End of quotation. It does not appear that it is an explanation of the first, nor a new sentence, because it would remain detached from what precedes it.

﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting⁠﴾: by sending the wind and the hosts, who were the angels, so there was no fighting between the believers and the disbelievers. It was also said: the intended ones are ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib and those with him, who came out for fighting and called to it. ʿAlī killed ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd (Wudd) from among the disbelievers in single combat, when ʿAmr sought single combat, and ʿAlī came out to him. ʿAmr said: "I do not wish to kill you because of my companionship with your father." ʿAlī said to him: "But I wish to kill you," and ʿAli killed him in single combat. Nawfal ibn al-Harith, of Quraysh, plunged into the trench with his horse and was killed there. Also killed from among the disbelievers were Munabbih ibn ʿUthman and ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbaq. Martyred from among the Muslims in the Battle of the Trench were: Muʿadh, Anas ibn Aws ibn ʿAtik, ʿAbdullah ibn Sahl, and Abu ʿAmr, who were from the Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal; al-Tufayl ibn al-Nuʿman and Thaʿlabah ibn Ghanamah, who were from the Banu Salamah; and Kaʿb ibn Zayd, from the Banu Dhubyan ibn al-Najjar, who was struck by a stray arrow and killed. Quraysh did not attack the Muslims after the Trench, and Allah sufficed them against the continuation and recurrence of fighting by defeating them afterward, and that was by His strength and might. It is related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: "We were detained on the day of the Trench, so we did not pray the noon prayer, nor the afternoon prayer, nor the sunset prayer, nor the night prayer, until after a portion of the night had passed, when we were relieved. Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting⁠﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then commanded Bilal, who gave the call to prayer and performed the noon prayer excellently, then each prayer after that with an iqamah."

And He brought down those who supported them (﴿وأنْزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهُمْ﴾), meaning those who aided the Quraysh and those with them among the confederates (al-Ahzab) from the People of the Book. They were the Jews of Banu Qurayzah, as the majority (al-Jumhur) hold. It is related from al-Hasan that they were Banu al-Nadir. The casting of terror was the cause of their coming down, but He mentioned the effect first, because the joy at their coming down was greater and the report of it was more important, so it was given precedence.

A man said: "O Messenger of God, Dihyah al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a silk saddle-cloth on it." He said: "That was Gabriel, peace be upon him, who was sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts."

When the confederates returned, Gabriel came at the time of noon and said: "God commands you to go out to Banu Qurayzah." So he called out among the people: "None of you shall pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." They set out for it. Some prayed on the road, and saw that this was meant as emphasis and urgency. Others prayed after the night prayer (al-'Isha'), and each was correct.

He besieged them for twenty-five nights. It is also said twenty-one, and it is also said fifteen. Then they came down under the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Awsi, because of an alliance that had existed between them, and they hoped for his kindness toward them. He judged that the fighting men should be killed, and the children, women and property should be taken as captives, and that the land and its produce should belong to the emigrants (al-Muhajirun) to the exclusion of the Helpers (al-Ansar). The Helpers spoke to him about this, and he said: "I wanted them to have property as you have." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "You have judged concerning them by the judgment of God from above the seven heavens." Then he had them brought down, and dug a trench for them in the marketplace of Madinah, and brought them forward and struck off their necks. They were between eight hundred and nine hundred. It is also said that there were six hundred fighting men and seven hundred captives.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadiri was brought, the one who had led them into treachery against the Messenger of God. He had entered among them out of loyalty to them, so he was left among those who were left to the judgment of Sa'd. When he drew near, wearing two garments of pale-yellow (tuffahiyyatan) cloth, his hands tied to his neck, he saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, by God, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes God will be forsaken." Then he said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of God and His decree, and it is a trial that was prescribed for the Children of Israel." Then he went forward and his neck was struck.

Someone from Banu Tha'labah said about him:
"By your life, the son of Akhtab did not blame himself,
but whoever forsakes God will be forsaken.
He strove until he had made his soul's excuse plain,
and he shook loose every one who seeks glory and stirs up strife."

He also killed one of their women, who was Lubabah, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had dropped a millstone on Khallad ibn Suwayd, and he was killed. No one other than him was martyred during the siege of Banu Qurayzah. Abu Sufyan ibn Mihsan, the brother of 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, died during the siege. The conquest of Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the fifth year after the Hijrah.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read (﴿وتَأْسِرُونَ﴾) "and you take captive" with the second-person ta' and a kasrah on the sin. Abu Haywah read both with a dammah. Al-Yamani read with the third-person ya'. Ibn Anas, on the authority of Ibn Dhakwan, read with the third-person ya' in both ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ وتَأْسِرُونَ﴾ (some you kill and some you take captive).

﴿وأوْرَثَكُمْ﴾ (and made you inherit) indicates that this passed to them after the death of those who were killed and of those who were removed from their land. It was mentioned first because of the great benefit of it from palm-groves and crops, and because they took possession of it a second time, along with their property, so that it might be used to strengthen the Muslims for jihad. It is also because it was in their houses, so the taking of possession of it was a third time.

﴿وأرْضًا لَمْ تَطَئُوها﴾ (and land you had not trodden) is a true promise of the opening of lands, such as Iraq, Syria, Yemen, Makkah, and all the other conquests of the Muslims. 'Ikrimah said: God informed them that He had decreed this. Al-Hasan said: He meant Rome and Persia. Qatadah said: "We used to say that it is Makkah." Muqatil, Yazid ibn Ruman and Ibn Zayd said: it is Khaybar. It is also said: Yemen. There is no basis for these specifications, and among the strange interpretations is that He meant their women.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿تَطَئُوها﴾ with a damma on the hamzah followed by a waw. Zayd ibn 'Ali read "lam tatuwha" (لَمْ تَطُوها) without the hamzah, changing the hamzah of "tata'u" into an alif, following the line of poetry:
"Indeed the beasts of prey lie still in their lairs,
but people are never guarded against their evil at all."
So the sakin alif met the waw and was dropped, as in your saying: "lam taraw-ha" (لَمْ تَرَوْها).

God concluded this verse with His power over everything, so nothing can overcome Him. This contained an indication of His granting the Muslims many conquests, and that He does not consider this unlikely. Just as He gave them possession of these, so He is able to give them possession of other lands.

(p-226)﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release.﴾ ﴿But if you desire God and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then God has prepared for those of you who do good a great reward.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold, and that is easy for God.﴾ ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are God-fearing, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire, but speak in a reasonable manner.﴾ ﴿And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the former time of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. God only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed God is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34] ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and women, the truthful men and women, the patient men and women, the humble men and women, the charitable men and women, the fasting men and women, the men and women who guard their private parts, and the men and women who remember God often: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

(p-227) The occasion of its revelation: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ became jealous of one another and desired an increase in clothing and maintenance, so this was revealed. When God granted victory to His Prophet, dispersed the confederates from him, and opened for him Quraydhah and al-Nadir, his wives thought that he had been given preference in the precious possessions and treasures of the Jews. So they sat around him and said: "O Messenger of God, the daughters of Kisra and Caesar have jewelry, fine garments, slave women and servants, while we are in the state of poverty and hardship that you see." They pained his heart by demanding that he widen their circumstances and that he treat them as kings and nobles treat their wives. So God commanded him to recite to them what had been revealed concerning their matter. At that time his wives were nine: ʿĀʾishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint ʿUmar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zamʿah, and Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; these were from Quraysh. From other than Quraysh: Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Khaybariyyah.

Abu al-Qasim al-Sayrafi said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ was given the choice between the kingdom of this world and the bliss of the Hereafter, he chose the Hereafter. He was commanded to offer his wives a choice so that the truthfulness of their agreement would become evident. He had ten wives, and he added al-Himyariyyah; they chose God and His Messenger, except al-Himyariyyah. It is narrated that he said to ʿĀʾishah, and he began with her, for she was the most beloved of them to him: "I am about to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm if you do not hasten in it until you consult your two parents." Then he recited the Qur'an to her. She said: "Concerning this should I consult my parents? Indeed I desire God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. Do not inform your wives that I have chosen you." He said: "Indeed God sent me as a conveyer of the message, and He did not send me as one who burdens others."

The apparent meaning is that if they choose the worldly life and its adornment, the Messenger of God ﷺ would provide for them and divorce them, and that the separation does not occur merely by their choosing it without him effecting it. Most scholars said: This is the verse of choice (takhyir). So when he says to her, "Choose," and she chooses her husband, that is not a divorce. It is narrated from ʿAli that she becomes one revocable divorce even if she chooses herself. According to Abu Hanifah and his companions, which is also the view of ʿAli, one irrevocable divorce occurs if she chooses herself; according to al-Shafiʿi, it is one revocable divorce, which is also the view of ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿud; according to Malik, it is three. Most people held that the verse concerns choice and divorce, which is the view of ʿAli, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. The speaker of this view said: As for the matter of divorce, it is deferred. If they choose themselves, he considers how he will release them, and there is no offer of choice in divorce in it, because choice implies three pronouncements of divorce, and he has said: "and release you with a fair release," and there is no fair release with an absolute final divorce. End of quotation.

What the apparent meaning of the verse indicates is what we mentioned first: that He made the granting of provision and release from Him contingent upon their desire for the adornment of the worldly life. The meaning of the verse is that their greatest concern and aim was to indulge in this world and attain its bliss and adornment.

The discussion of ﴿fa-taʿālayna﴾ has already been covered in His saying: ﴿Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons﴾ [Al ʿImran: 61] in Al ʿImran.

﴿Umattiʿkunna﴾: It was said that providing (mutʿah) is obligatory in divorce; it was also said that it is recommended. The command in His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236] requires obligation according to the jurists' school, and the discussion of this and the detailed positions were covered in al-Baqarah. The fair release (tasrih jamil) is either a release without harm to the house, or fair praise, good belief, and good companionship if it is complete. The majority read ﴿umattiʿkunna﴾ with shaddah from matta; Zayd ibn ʿAli read it without shaddah from amtaʿa. The meaning of (aʿadda) is "prepared and facilitated." He used the apparent noun in place of the pronoun to draw attention to the attribute by which the great reward is merited for them, which is good-doing (ihsan), as if He said: "He prepared it for you," because whoever desires God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode is a doer of good. The reading of Humayd al-Kharraz: ﴿umattiʿkunna wa-usarriḥkunna﴾ with raf (damma) is an istiʾnaf (resumed new sentence); the majority read with jazm (sukun) as a response to the command, or as a response to the condition, and ﴿fa-taʿālayna﴾ would then be a parenthetical clause (jumlat iʿtirad) between the condition and its consequence, and the entry of the fa' upon a parenthetical clause does no harm. A similar example is the poet's saying:

"Know that the knowledge of a man benefits him: that everything decreed will certainly come."

Then He addressed the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, so that they would give attention to what they are addressed with, since it is a matter deserving attention. Zayd ibn ʿAli, (p-228) al-Jahdari, ʿAmr ibn Fa'id al-Aswari, and Yaʿqub read ﴿ta'ti﴾ with the feminine ta' (taʾnith), taking account of the meaning of man; the majority read it with the yaʾ, taking account of the wording of man.

﴿bi-fahishatin mubayyinah﴾: a grave sin among the sins. It should not be supposed that it is fornication, because of the infallibility of the Messenger of God ﷺ from that, and because He described it as clear, while fornication is something concealed. The indecency should rather be understood as disobedience to the husband and corruption of companionship. Since their dwelling was the place of descent of revelation of commands and prohibitions, this obligated them more because of that, and because they were under the Messenger ﷺ more than others would be, so their reward and punishment were doubled. Nafiʿ, Hamzah, ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ with an alif and a fatha on the ʿayn; al-Hasan, ʿIsa, and Abu ʿAmr read it with shaddah and fatha on the ʿayn; al-Jahdari, Ibn Kathir, and Abu ʿAmir read it with nun and shaddah with kasrah on the ʿayn; Zayd ibn ʿAli, Ibn Muhaysin, and Kharijah from Abu ʿAmr read it with alif, nun, and kasrah; and a group read it with the yaʾ of the third person and alif and kasrah. Whoever reads the ʿayn with fatha makes (al-ʿadhab) (the punishment) raf' (nominative); whoever reads it with kasrah makes it nasb (accusative).

﴿ḍiʿfayn﴾: that is, two punishments, so another punishment is added to the punishment of the rest of people. Abu ʿUbaydah and Abu ʿAmr, as related by al-Tabari from them, said: Two punishments are added to the punishment, making three. The doubling of the reward after this statement is because the punishment for indecency corresponds to the reward for obedience.

﴿wa-kana dhalika﴾: that is, the doubling of punishment upon them ﴿ʿala Allahi yasiran﴾: easy, facile. In this is an announcement that being women, together with committing sin, does not avail them anything, and that it is the cause of doubling the punishment.

﴿wa-man yaqnut﴾: that is, obeys and submits with servitude to God and with agreement with His Messenger. The majority read ﴿wa-man yaqnut﴾ in the masculine, taking account of the wording of "man," and ﴿taʿmal﴾ with ta' taking account of the meaning.

﴿nu'tiha﴾ with the nun of majesty. Al-Jahdari, al-Aswari, Yaʿqub in one narration read ﴿wa-man taqnut﴾ with ta' of the feminine, taking account of the meaning; Ibn ʿAmir also read it that way in one narration, and Abu Hatim narrated it from Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, and Nafiʿ. Ibn Khalawayh said: I have not heard that anyone read ﴿wa-man yaqnut﴾ except with ta'. Al-Sulami, Ibn Wathhab, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read all three with yaʾ from below. Abu al-Baqa mentioned that some read ﴿wa-man yaqnut﴾ with yaʾ, taking account of the meaning, and ﴿ya'mal﴾ with yaʾ, taking account of the wording of "man." Some grammarians said: This is weak, because the masculine is the root and is not made subordinate to the feminine; and what they gave as a reason for it has come in the Qur'an similarly, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Pure for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾ [al-Anʿam: 139]. End of quotation. The discussion of (khalisah) was already covered in al-Anʿam. The generous provision (rizq karim) is Paradise. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: It is possible that in this there is a worldly promise, meaning that their provisions in this world are upon God, and it is generous in that it is lawful and intended, and with God's pleasure in attaining it. Some commentators said: The punishment threatened for them, double, is the punishment of this world and then the punishment of the Hereafter; and likewise the reward, and this is weak. End of quotation. Their reward was doubled only because they sought the pleasure of the Messenger of God ﷺ through good character, pleasant companionship, contentment, and devotion to the worship of God.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women﴾: that is, not every one of you is like a single person among women, meaning among the women of your age. The negation is not directed at the comparison in being women. You say: "Zayd is not like any of the people," not intending the negation of resemblance in being human, but in a more specific attribute existing in him, which is being knowledgeable, or active, or praying. So the meaning is: there exists in you a distinction that does not exist in others, which is that you are the mothers of the believers and wives of the best of messengers. The Qur'an was revealed concerning you. Just as he, peace be upon him, is not like any of the men, as he, peace be upon him, said: "I am not like any of you," so too his wives who were honored by him. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Ahad" originally has the meaning of "wahid," meaning "one"; then it was placed in general negation, in which the masculine, the feminine, the singular, and what is beyond it are equal. The meaning is: you are not like one group among the groups of women; that is, if you trace the nation of women group by group, you will not find one group among them that equals you in merit and precedence. From it is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those who believe in God and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them﴾ [al-Nisa': 152], meaning between one group of them, making equal all of them in that they are upon the manifest truth. End of quotation.

As for his saying that "ahad" originally means "wahad," which is "one," this is correct. As for his saying "then it was placed" up to "and what is beyond it," this is not correct, because what is used in general negation has a meaning different from the meaning of "wahid," since "wahid" applies to anything characterized by unity, whereas "ahad" used in general negation is specific to rational beings. The grammarians mentioned that its root is hamzah, ha', and dal, while the root of "ahad" in the sense of "wahad" originally is waw, ha', and dal; so they differ in root and in meaning. As for his saying ﴿you are not﴾ like one group, we have said that His saying ﴿you are not﴾ means: not every one of you is such; it is a judgment on each one individually, not a judgment on the collective as collective. We have said that the meaning of ﴿like any one﴾ is: like a single person, so we kept "ahad" in its original masculine form and did not interpret it as a single group. As for ﴿and do not differentiate between any of them﴾ [al-Nisa': 152], the "ahad" there may be the one used for general negation, and for this reason it came in a negative context, so it became general, and the preposition "bayn" is suitable for generality. It is also possible that "ahad" means "wahid," and that a conjunction has been omitted, meaning "between one and another of His messengers," as the poet said:

"Had Abu Hajar come back safe, there would not have been between the good and him except a few nights."

Ibn 'Atiyya...

Actually, the passage begins with the commentary's own text, so here is the translation:

أيْ: لَسْتُنَّ مِثْلَهُنَّ إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ اللَّهَ، وذَلِكَ لَمّا انْضافَ مَعَ تَقْوى اللَّهِ مِن صُحْبَةِ الرَّسُولِ ﷺ وعَظِيمِ المَحَلِّ مِنهُ، ونُزُولِ القُرْآنِ في بَيْتِهِنَّ وفي حَقِّهِنَّ.

That is: "You are not like any other women if you fear Allah," because to the fear of Allah was added companionship with the Messenger (ﷺ), his great station with him, and the revelation of the Qur'an in your houses and concerning you.

وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: ﴿إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ﴾ إنْ أرَدْتُنَّ التَّقْوى، وإنْ كُنَّ مُتَّقِياتٍ.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "﴿If you fear [Allah]﴾ means if you intend piety, and [it also means] if you are already pious."

﴿فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ بِالقَوْلِ﴾ فَلا تُجِبْنَ بِقَوْلِكُنَّ خاضِعًا، أيْ: لَيِّنًا خَنِثًا، مِثْلَ كَلامِ المُرِيباتِ والمُومِساتِ.

﴿So do not be soft in speech﴾ means do not answer with speech that is submissive, that is, soft and suggestive, like the speech of women who arouse suspicion and of prostitutes.

﴿فَيَطْمَعَ الَّذِي في قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾ أيْ: رِيبَةً وفُجُورًا. انْتَهى. فَعَلى القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ يَكُونُ ﴿إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ﴾ قَيْدًا في كَوْنِهِنَّ لَسْنَ كَأحَدٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ، ويَكُونُ جَوابُ الشَّرْطِ مَحْذُوفًا. وعَلى ما قالَهُ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ، يَكُونُ ﴿إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ﴾ ابْتِداءَ شَرْطٍ، وجَوابُهُ ﴿فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ﴾ وكِلا القَوْلَيْنِ فِيهِما حُمِلَ.

﴿So that he in whose heart is a disease may not be tempted﴾ means: doubt and immorality. End of quote. According to the first view, ﴿if you fear [Allah]﴾ is a restriction on their not being like any of the women, and the answer to the condition is omitted. According to what al-Zamakhshari said, ﴿if you fear﴾ is the beginning of a conditional clause whose answer is ﴿do not be soft﴾. Both views have been reported regarding these words.

﴿إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ﴾ عَلى تَقْوى اللَّهِ تَعالى، وهو ظاهِرُ الِاسْتِعْمالِ، وعِنْدِي أنَّهُ مَحْمُولٌ عَلى أنَّ مَعْناهُ: إنِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُنَّ أحَدًا ﴿فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ﴾ . واتَّقى بِمَعْنى: اسْتَقْبَلَ مَعْرُوفٌ في اللُّغَةِ، قالَ النّابِغَةُ:

﴿If you fear﴾ refers to the fear of Allah the Exalted, and this is the apparent usage. In my view, however, it means: if you face anyone, ﴿then do not be soft﴾. The use of ittaqa in the sense of "to face" is well known in the language. Al-Nabigha said:

؎سَقَطَ النَّصِيفُ ولَمْ تُرِدْ إسْقاطَهُ ∗∗∗ فَتَناوَلَتْهُ واتَّقَتْنا بِاليَدِ

"The veil fell, though she did not intend to let it fall, so she caught it and shielded herself from us with her hand."

أيِ: اسْتَقْبَلَتْنا بِاليَدِ، ويَكُونُ هَذا المَعْنى أبْلَغَ في مَدْحِهِنَّ، إذْ لَمْ يُعَلِّقْ فَضِيلَتَهُنَّ عَلى التَّقْوى، ولا عَلَّقَ نَهْيَهُنَّ عَنِ الخُضُوعِ بِها، إذْ هُنَّ مُتَّقِياتٌ لِلَّهِ في أنْفُسِهِنَّ، والتَّعْلِيقُ يَقْتَضِي ظاهِرُهُ أنَّهُنَّ لَسْنَ مُتَحَلِّياتٍ بِالتَّقْوى.

That is: she met us with her hand. This meaning is more eloquent in praising them, since it does not make their excellence depend on piety, nor make the prohibition against softness depend on it, because they are already God-fearing in themselves. Whereas the conditional, in its apparent sense, implies that they were not adorned with piety.

قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: لا تُرَخِّصْنَ بِالقَوْلِ. وقالَ الحَسَنُ: لا تَكَلَّمْنَ بِالرَّفَثِ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: لا تَكَلَّمْنَ بِما يَهْوى المُرِيبُ. وقالَ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ: الخُضُوعُ بِالقَوْلِ ما يُدْخِلُ في القَلْبِ الغَزَلَ. وقِيلَ: لا تُلِنَّ لِلرِّجالِ القَوْلَ.

Ibn 'Abbas said: do not speak in a lax manner. Al-Hasan said: do not speak with lewd talk. Al-Kalbi said: do not speak in a way that pleases the one who is doubtful. Ibn Zayd said: submissive speech is that which introduces amorous flirtation into the heart. It was also said: do not soften your speech to men.

أمَرَ تَعالى أنْ يَكُونَ الكَلامُ خَيْرًا، لا عَلى وجْهٍ يُظْهِرُ في القَلْبِ عَلاقَةَ ما يَظْهَرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اللِّينِ، كَما كانَ الحالُ عَلَيْهِ في نِساءِ العَرَبِ مِن مُكالَمَةِ الرِّجالِ بِرَخِيمِ الصَّوْتِ ولَيِّنِهِ، مِثْلَ كَلامِ المُومِساتِ، فَنَهاهُنَّ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وقالَ الشّاعِرُ:

Allah the Exalted commanded that speech be proper, not in a way that reveals in the heart an attachment arising from the softness it displays, as was the case with the women of the Arabs who spoke with men in a soft, languid voice, like the speech of prostitutes. So He forbade them from that. The poet said:

؎بِتَكَلُّمٍ لَوْ تَسْتَطِيعُ كَلامَهُ ∗∗∗ لَدَنَتْ لَهُ أرْوى الهِضابِ الصُّخَّدِ

"With a speech whose words, if you could, would make the mountain-goats of the rugged hills draw near to him."

وقالَ آخَرُ:

Another said:

؎لَوْ أنَّها عَرَضَتْ لِأشْمَطَ راهِبٍ ∗∗∗ عَبَدَ الإلَهَ صَرُورَةٍ مُتَعَبِّدِ
؎لَرَنا لِرُؤْيَتِها وحُسْنِ حَدِيثِها ∗∗∗ ولَخالَهُ رُشْدًا وإنْ لَمْ يَرْشُدِ

"Even if she appeared before a grey-haired monk who worships God, celibate and devoted, he would gaze at her with longing and at the beauty of her speech, and would take it for right guidance, even though he was not guided."

(p-٢٣٠)وقَرَأ الجُمْهُورُ: ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ﴾ بِفَتْحِ المِيمِ ونَصْبِ العَيْنِ، جَوابًا لِلنَّهْيِ؛ وأبانُ بْنُ عُثْمانَ، وابْنُ هُرْمُزَ: بِالجَزْمِ، فَكُسِرَتِ العَيْنُ لِالتِقاءِ السّاكِنَيْنِ، نُهِينَ عَنِ الخُضُوعِ بِالقَوْلِ، ونُهِيَ مَرِيضُ القَلْبِ عَنِ الطَّمَعِ، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: لا تَخْضَعْ فَلا تَطْمَعْ. وقِراءَةُ النَّصْبِ أبْلَغُ؛ لِأنَّها تَقْتَضِي الخُضُوعَ بِسَبَبِ الطَّمَعِ.

(p-230) The majority read ﴿fa-yatma'a﴾ with a fatha on the mim and a fatha on the 'ayn, as a response to the prohibition. Aban ibn 'Uthman and Ibn Hurmuz read it with a jazm (jussive), so the 'ayn was kasra because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters. The women are forbidden from softness in speech, and the one with a diseased heart is forbidden from desire, as if it were said: do not be soft, so that he does not desire. The fatha reading is more eloquent, because it implies softness on account of desire.

وقالَ أبُو عُمَرٍو الدّانِيُّ: قَرَأ الأعْرَجُ وعِيسى: ”فَيَطْمِعَ“، بِفَتْحِ الياءِ وكَسْرِ المِيمِ. ونَقَلَها ابْنُ خالَوَيْهِ عَنْ أبِي السِّماكِ، قالَ: وقَدْ رُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ مُحَيْصِنٍ، وذَكَرَ أنَّ الأعْرَجَ، وهو ابْنُ هُرْمُزَ، قَرَأ: ”فَيُطْمِعَ“، بِضَمِّ الياءِ وفَتْحِ العَيْنِ وكَسْرِ المِيمِ، أيْ: فَيَطْمَعُ هو، أيِ: الخُضُوعُ بِالقَوْلِ؛ و(الَّذِي) مَفْعُولٌ، أوِ (الَّذِي) فاعِلٌ والمَفْعُولُ مَحْذُوفٌ، أيْ: فَيَطْمَعُ نَفْسُهُ. والمَرَضُ، قالَ قَتادَةُ: النِّفاقُ؛ وقالَ عِكْرِمَةُ: الفِسْقُ والغَزَلُ.

Abu 'Amr al-Dani said: al-A'raj and 'Isa read ﴿fa-yut'ima﴾ with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the mim. Ibn Khalawayh transmitted it from Abu al-Samak, and said: it has also been reported from Ibn Muhaysin. He mentioned that al-A'raj, who is Ibn Hurmuz, read ﴿fa-yut'ima﴾ with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the 'ayn and a kasra on the mim, meaning: he (the softness of speech) makes him desire, and ﴿alladhi﴾ is the object, or ﴿alladhi﴾ is the subject and the object is omitted, meaning: his own self desires. As for "disease," Qatada said: hypocrisy; 'Ikrima said: immorality and flirtation.

﴿وقُلْنَ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ والمُحَرَّمُ، وهو الَّذِي لا تُنْكِرُهُ الشَّرِيعَةُ ولا العُقُولُ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: المَرْأةُ تَنْدُبُ إذا خالَطَتِ الأجانِبَ، عَلَيْها بِالمُصاهَرَةِ إلى الغِلْظَةِ في القَوْلِ مِن غَيْرِ رَفْعِ الصَّوْتِ، فَإنَّها مَأْمُورَةٌ بِخَفْضِ الكَلامِ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: مَعْرُوفًا صَحِيحًا، بِلا هَجَرٍ ولا تَمْرِيضٍ. وقالَ الضَّحّاكُ: عَنِيفًا؛ وقِيلَ: خَشِنًا حَسَنًا؛ وقِيلَ: مَعْرُوفًا، أيْ: قَوْلًا أُذِنَ لَكم فِيهِ؛ وقِيلَ: ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ وما يُحْتاجُ إلَيْهِ مِنَ الكَلامِ.

﴿And speak a known word﴾ means the permitted, that which neither the Sharia nor reason rejects. Ibn 'Abbas said: a woman should speak with a firm tone when she mixes with strangers, for the in-laws... [as the text reads] ...for she is commanded to lower her speech. Al-Kalbi said: "known" means sound, without abuse or hinting at illness. Al-Dahhak said: harsh. It was said: rough but good. It was said: "known" means words you have been permitted to say. It was said: the remembrance of Allah and whatever speech one needs.

وقَرَأ الجُمْهُورُ: ”وقِرْنَ“، بِكَسْرِ القافِ، مِن وقَرَ يَقِرُ إذا سَكَنَ وأصْلُهُ: أوْقِرْنَ، مِثْلُ عِدْنَ مِن وعَدَ. وذَكَرَ أبُو الفَتْحِ الهَمْدانِيُّ، في كِتابِ التِّبْيانِ، وجْهًا آخَرَ قالَ: قارَّ يَقارُّ، إذا اجْتَمَعَ، ومِنهُ القارَّةُ لِاجْتِماعِها. ألا تَرى إلى قَوْلِ عُضَلَ والدِّيشِ: اجْتَمِعُوا فَكُونُوا قارَّةً ؟ فالمَعْنى: اجْمَعْنَ أنْفُسَكُنَّ في بُيُوتِكُنَّ.

The majority read ﴿waqirna﴾ with a kasra on the qaf, from waqara yaqiru, meaning to be still; its origin is ﴿awqirna﴾, like ﴿idna﴾ from wa'ada. Abu al-Fath al-Hamadani, in his book al-Tibyan, mentioned another way: qarra yaqarru, meaning to gather, from which comes al-qarra (the group), because of its gathering. Do you not see the saying of 'Udal and al-Dish: "Gather together and become a group"? The meaning is: gather yourselves in your houses.

﴿وقَرْنَ﴾ [الأحزاب: ٣٣] أمْرٌ مِن قارَ، كَما تَقُولُ: خِفْنَ مِن خافَ؛ أوْ مِنَ القَرارِ، تَقُولُ: قَرَرْتُ بِالمَكانِ، وأصْلُهُ: واقْرِرْنَ، حُذِفَتِ الرّاءُ الثّانِيَةُ تَخْفِيفًا، كَما حَذَفُوا لامَ ظَلِلْتُ، ثُمَّ نُقِلَتْ حَرَكَتُها إلى القافِ فَذَهَبَتْ ألِفُ الوَصْلِ. وقالَ أبُو عَلِيٍّ: أُبْدِلَتِ الرّاءُ ونُقِلَتْ حَرَكَتُها إلى القافِ، ثُمَّ حُذِفَتِ الياءُ لِسُكُونِها وسُكُونِ الرّاءِ بَعْدَها. انْتَهى، وهَذا غايَةٌ في التَّحْمِيلِ كَعادَتِهِ.

﴿Waqarna﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] is an imperative from qara, just as one says khifna from khafa. Or it is from al-qarar (settling), as one says qarartu bi-al-makan (I settled in the place). Its origin is ﴿waqrirna﴾; the second ra' was deleted for lightness, as they deleted the lam of zalaltu. Then its vowel was moved to the qaf, and the alif of connection was dropped. Abu 'Ali said: the ra' was replaced, its vowel moved to the qaf, then the ya' was deleted because it was unvocalized and the ra' after it was also unvocalized. End of quote; this is an extreme of over-analysis, as is his habit.

وقَرَأ عاصِمٌ ونافِعٌ: بِفَتْحِ القافِ، وهي لُغَةُ العَرَبِ؛ يَقُولُونَ: قَرِرْتُ بِالمَكانِ، بِكَسْرِ الرّاءِ وبِفَتْحِ القافِ، حَكاهُ أبُو عُبَيْدٍ والزَّجّاجُ وغَيْرُهُما، وأنْكَرَها قَوْمٌ، مِنهُمُ المازِنِيُّ، وقالُوا: بِكَسْرِ الرّاءِ، مِن قَرَّتِ العَيْنُ، وبِفَتْحِها مِنَ القَرارِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ أبِي عَبْلَةَ: ”واقْرِرْنَ“، بِألِفِ الوَصْلِ وكَسْرِ الرّاءِ الأُولى. وتَقَدَّمَ لَنا الكَلامُ عَلى قَرِرْتُ، وأنَّهُ بِالفَتْحِ والكَسْرِ مِنَ القَرارِ ومِنَ القِرَّةِ.

Asim and Nafi' read with a fatha on the qaf, which is the dialect of the Arabs; they say qarirtu bi-al-makan, with a kasra on the ra' and a fatha on the qaf. This was related by Abu 'Ubayd, al-Zajjaj and others, but some rejected it, among them al-Mazini, who said: [it is] with a kasra on the ra', from qarrat al-'ayn (the eye became cool), and with a fatha from al-qarar. Ibn Abi Abla read ﴿waqrirna﴾ with an alif of connection and a kasra on the first ra'. We have already discussed qarirtu, and that with a fatha and kasra it comes from al-qarar and from al-qirra.

أمَرَهُنَّ تَعالى بِمُلازَمَةِ بُيُوتِهِنَّ، ونَهاهُنَّ عَنِ التَّبَرُّجِ، وأعْلَمَ تَعالى أنَّهُ فِعْلُ الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى، وكانَتْ عائِشَةُ إذا قَرَأتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ بَكَتْ حَتّى تَبُلَّ خِمارَها، تَتَذَكَّرُ خُرُوجَها أيّامَ الجَمَلِ تَطْلُبُ بِدَمِ عُثْمانَ. وقِيلَ لِسَوْدَةَ: لِمَ لا تَحُجِّينَ وتَعْتَمِرِينَ كَما يَفْعَلُ إخْوانُكِ ؟ فَقالَتْ: قَدْ حَجَجْتُ واعْتَمَرْتُ وأمَرَنِي اللَّهُ أنْ أقِرَّ في بَيْتِي، فَما خَرَجَتْ مِن بابِ حُجْرَتِها حَتّى أُخْرِجَتْ جِنازَتُها.

Allah the Exalted commanded them to remain in their houses, forbade them from tabarruj (displaying their beauty), and informed them that it is the act of the first jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam). 'Aisha, whenever she recited this verse, would weep until her veil was soaked, remembering her going out in the days of the Camel, seeking the blood of 'Uthman. It was said to Sawda: "Why do you not perform the Hajj and 'Umrah as your brothers do?" She said: "I have performed Hajj and 'Umrah, and Allah has commanded me to remain in my house." She did not leave the door of her chamber until her funeral was carried out.

﴿ولا تَبَرَّجْنَ﴾ [الأحزاب: ٣٣] قالَ مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ: التَّبَرُّجُ: التَّبَخْتُرُ والتَّغَنُّجُ والتَّكَسُّرُ. وقالَ مُقاتِلٌ: تُلْقِي الخِمارَ عَلى وجْهِها ولا تَشُدُّهُ. وقالَ المُبَرِّدُ: تُبْدِي مِن مَحاسِنِها ما يَجِبُ عَلَيْها سَتْرُهُ.

﴿And do not display yourselves [tabarruj]﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Mujahid and Qatada said: tabarruj is strutting, coquetry and affected softness. Muqatil said: she throws her veil over her face without fastening it. Al-Mubarrad said: she reveals from her beauty what it is obligatory for her to conceal.

و﴿الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى﴾ [الأحزاب: ٣٣] يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ ثَمَّ جاهِلِيَّةٌ مُتَقَدِّمَةٌ وأُخْرى مُتَأخِّرَةٌ. فَقِيلَ: هُما ابْنانِ لِآدَمَ، سَكَنَ أحَدُهُما الجَبَلَ، فَذُكُورُ أوْلادِهِ صِباحٌ وإناثُهم قِباحٌ؛ والآخَرُ السَّهْلَ، وأوْلادُهُ عَلى عَكْسِ ذَلِكَ. فَسَوّى لَهم إبْلِيسُ عِيدًا يَجْتَمِعُ جَمِيعُهم فِيهِ، فَمالَ ذُكُورُ الجَبَلِ إلى إناثِ السَّهْلِ وبِالعَكْسِ، فَكَثُرَتِ الفاحِشَةُ، فَهو تَبَرُّجُ الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى.

﴿The first jahiliyya﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] indicates that there was an earlier jahiliyya and a later one. It was said: they are two sons of Adam. One of them lived in the mountain, so the males of his offspring were handsome and the females ugly; the other lived in the plain, and his offspring were the reverse. Iblis arranged for them a festival in which all of them gathered, and the males of the mountain inclined toward the females of the plain and vice versa, so immorality increased. This is the tabarruj of the first jahiliyya.

وقالَ عِكْرِمَةُ والحَكَمُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ: ما بَيْنَ آدَمَ ونُوحٍ، وهي ثَمانُمِائَةِ سَنَةٍ، كانَ الرِّجالُ صِباحًا والنِّساءُ قِباحًا، فَكانَتِ المَرْأةُ تَدْعُو الرَّجُلَ إلى نَفْسِها. وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا: الجاهِلِيَّةُ الأُولى ما بَيْنَ إدْرِيسَ ونُوحٍ، كانَتْ ألْفَ سَنَةٍ، تَجْمَعُ المَرْأةُ بَيْنَ زَوْجٍ وعَشِيقٍ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ وغَيْرُهُ: ما بَيْنَ نُوحٍ وإبْراهِيمَ. قالَ مُقاتِلٌ: زَمَنَ نُمْرُوذَ، بَغايا يَلْبَسْنَ أرَقَّ الدُّرُوعِ ويَمْشِينَ في الطُّرُقِ.

'Ikrima and al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna said: it is the period between Adam and Noah, which is eight hundred years; the men were handsome and the women ugly, so a woman would invite a man to herself. Ibn 'Abbas also said: the first jahiliyya was between Idris and Noah, and it lasted a thousand years; a woman would combine a husband and a lover. Al-Kalbi and others said: it is between Noah and Abraham. Muqatil said: in the time of Nimrod, there were prostitutes who wore the thinnest coats of mail and walked in the streets.

وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: والجاهِلِيَّةُ الأُولى هي القَدِيمَةُ الَّتِي يُقالُ لَها الجاهِلِيَّةُ الجَهْلاءُ، (p-٢٣١)وهِيَ الزَّمانُ الَّذِي وُلِدَ فِيهِ إبْراهِيمُ. كانَتِ المَرْأةُ تَلْبَسُ الدِّرْعَ مِنَ اللُّؤْلُؤِ، فَتَمْشِي وسَطَ الطَّرِيقِ تَعْرِضُ نَفْسَها عَلى الرِّجالِ. وقالَ أبُو العالِيَةِ: مِن داوُدَ وسُلَيْمانَ، كانَ لِلْمَرْأةِ قَمِيصٌ مِنَ الدُّرِّ غَيْرُ مَخِيطِ الجانِبَيْنِ، يَظْهَرُ مِنهُ الأكْعابُ والسَّوْأتانِ.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the first jahiliyya is the ancient one, called the "ignorant jahiliyya," (p-231) which is the time in which Abraham was born. A woman would wear a coat of mail made of pearls and walk in the middle of the road, displaying herself to men. Abu al-'Aliya said: from the time of David and Solomon, a woman had a shirt of pearls, unstitched at the sides, through which her ankles and private parts would show.

وقالَ المُبَرِّدُ: كانَتِ المَرْأةُ تَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ زَوْجِها وخِلْمِها، لِلزَّوْجِ نِصْفُها الأسْفَلُ، ولِلْخِلْمِ نِصْفُها، يَتَمَتَّعُ بِهِ في التَّقْبِيلِ والتَّرَشُّفِ. وقِيلَ: ما بَيْنَ مُوسى وعِيسى. وقالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ: ما بَيْنَ عِيسى ومُحَمَّدٍ، عَلَيْهِما الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ. وقالَ مُقاتِلٌ: الأُولى زَمَنُ إبْراهِيمَ، والثّانِيَةُ زَمَنَ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ قَبْلَ أنْ يُبْعَثَ،

Al-Mubarrad said: a woman would combine her husband and her lover; the husband had her lower half and the lover had her upper half, enjoying her through kissing and sipping. It was said: it is between Moses and Jesus. Al-Sha'bi said: between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. Muqatil said: the first is the time of Abraham, and the second is the time of Muhammad (peace be upon him) before he was sent as a prophet.

وقالَ الزَّجّاجُ: الأشْبَهُ قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ لِأنَّهم هُمُ الجاهِلِيَّةُ المَعْرُوفُونَ كانُوا يَتَّخِذُونَ البَغايا، وإنَّما قِيلَ: الأُولى؛ لِأنَّهُ يُقالُ لِكُلِّ مُتَقَدِّمٍ ومُتَقَدِّمَةٍ: أوَّلُ وأُولى، وتَأْوِيلُهُ أنَّهم تَقَدَّمُوا عَلى أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ فَهم أُولى وهم أوَّلُ مِن أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ، وقالَ عُمَرُ لِابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: وهَلْ كانَتِ الجاهِلِيَّةُ إلّا واحِدَةً ؟ فَقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: وهَلْ كانَتِ الأُولى إلّا ولَها آخِرَةٌ ؟ فَقالَ عُمَرُ: لِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ يا ابْنَ عَبّاسٍ.

Al-Zajjaj said: the view of al-Sha'bi is more plausible, because they are the well-known jahiliyya, who used to take prostitutes. The word "first" is used because one says "awwal" and "ula" for every earlier thing; its explanation is that they preceded the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), so they are the "first," and they are the earlier part of the community of Muhammad, peace be upon him. 'Umar said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Was the jahiliyya anything but one?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Was the first anything but one that has a last?" 'Umar said: "By Allah, how well you have said it, Ibn 'Abbas."

وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: والجاهِلِيَّةُ الأُخْرى ما بَيْنَ عِيسى ومُحَمَّدٍ، عَلَيْهِما الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ الجاهِلِيَّةُ الأُولى جاهِلِيَّةَ الكُفْرِ قَبْلَ الإسْلامِ، والجاهِلِيَّةُ الأُخْرى جاهِلِيَّةَ الفُسُوقِ والفُجُورِ في الإسْلامِ، فَكانَ المَعْنى: ولا يَجِدُكُنَّ بِالتَّبَرُّجِ جاهِلِيَّةً في الإسْلامِ يَتَشَبَّهْنَ بِها بِأهْلِ جاهِلِيَّةِ الكُفْرِ. ويُعَضِّدُهُ ما رُوِيَ أنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قالَ لِأبِي الدَّرْداءِ: «إنَّ فِيكَ جاهِلِيَّةً ”، قالَ: جاهِلِيَّةُ كُفْرٍ أمْ إسْلامٍ ؟ فَقالَ:“ بَلْ جاهِلِيَّةُ كُفْرٍ ”» . انْتَهى.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the second jahiliyya is between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. It is also possible that the first jahiliyya is the jahiliyya of disbelief before Islam, and the second jahiliyya is the jahiliyya of wickedness and immorality within Islam. The meaning would then be: do not let tabarruj find you as a jahiliyya within Islam, imitating the people of the jahiliyya of disbelief. This is supported by what is reported: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Darda: "Indeed, there is jahiliyya in you." He said: "Is it jahiliyya of disbelief or of Islam?" He said: "Rather, it is jahiliyya of disbelief." End of quote.

والمَعْرُوفُ في الحَدِيثِ أنَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ إنَّما قالَ:“ «إنَّكَ امْرُؤٌ فِيكَ جاهِلِيَّةٌ»، لِأبِي ذَرٍّ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

The well-known hadith is that the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "You are a man in whom there is jahiliyya," to Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).

وقالَ ابْنُ عَطِيَّةَ: والَّذِي يَظْهَرُ عِنْدِي أنَّهُ أشارَ إلى الجاهِلِيَّةِ الَّتِي يَخُصُّها، فَأُمِرْنَ بِالنُّقْلَةِ مِن سِيرَتِهِنَّ فِيها، وهي ما كانَ قَبْلَ الشَّرْعِ مِن سِيرَةِ الكُفْرِ، ولِأنَّهم كانُوا لا غَيْرَةَ عِنْدَهم، وكانَ أمْرُ النِّساءِ دُونَ حَجَبَةٍ، وجَعَلَها أوْلى بِالإضافَةِ إلى حالَةِ الإسْلامِ، ولَيْسَ المَعْنى أنَّ ثَمَّ جاهِلِيَّةٌ أُخْرى. وقَدْ مَرَّ إطْلاقُ اسْمِ الجاهِلِيَّةِ عَلى تِلْكَ المُدَّةِ الَّتِي قَبْلَ الإسْلامِ، فَقالُوا: جاهِلِيٌّ في الشُّعَراءِ. وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ في البُخارِيِّ: سَمِعْتُ، أيْ: في الجاهِلِيَّةِ إلى غَيْرِ هَذا. انْتَهى.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: what appears to me is that it refers to the particular jahiliyya that is specific to them, from which they were commanded to move away in their conduct: that is, the conduct of disbelief before the Sharia, and because they had no jealousy, and the matter of women was without veiling. He made it "first" in relation to the state of Islam, and the meaning is not that there is another jahiliyya. The name jahiliyya has already been applied to that period before Islam; they said: "jahili" among the poets. Ibn 'Abbas said in al-Bukhari: "I heard..." that is, in the jahiliyya, to other than this. End of quote.

(p-226)﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release.﴾ ﴿But if you desire God and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then God has prepared for those of you who do good a great reward.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear indecency, her punishment will be doubled twofold, and that is easy for God.﴾ ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are God-fearing, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should feel desire, but speak in a reasonable manner.﴾ ﴿And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the former time of ignorance. Establish prayer, give zakah, and obey God and His Messenger. God only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with complete purification.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33] ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed God is ever Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34] ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and women, the truthful men and women, the patient men and women, the humble men and women, the charitable men and women, the fasting men and women, the men and women who guard their private parts, and the men and women who remember God often: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

(p-227) The occasion of its revelation: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ became jealous of one another and desired an increase in clothing and maintenance, so this was revealed. When God granted victory to His Prophet, dispersed the confederates from him, and opened for him Quraydhah and al-Nadir, his wives thought that he had been given preference in the precious possessions and treasures of the Jews. So they sat around him and said: "O Messenger of God, the daughters of Kisra and Caesar have jewelry, fine garments, slave women and servants, while we are in the state of poverty and hardship that you see." They pained his heart by demanding that he widen their circumstances and that he treat them as kings and nobles treat their wives. So God commanded him to recite to them what had been revealed concerning their matter. At that time his wives were nine: ʿĀʾishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint ʿUmar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zamʿah, and Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah; these were from Quraysh. From other than Quraysh: Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah, and Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Khaybariyyah.

Abu al-Qasim al-Sayrafi said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ was given the choice between the kingdom of this world and the bliss of the Hereafter, he chose the Hereafter. He was commanded to offer his wives a choice so that the truthfulness of their agreement would become evident. He had ten wives, and he added al-Himyariyyah; they chose God and His Messenger, except al-Himyariyyah. It is narrated that he said to ʿĀʾishah, and he began with her, for she was the most beloved of them to him: "I am about to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm if you do not hasten in it until you consult your two parents." Then he recited the Qur'an to her. She said: "Concerning this should I consult my parents? Indeed I desire God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. Do not inform your wives that I have chosen you." He said: "Indeed God sent me as a conveyer of the message, and He did not send me as one who burdens others."

The apparent meaning is that if they choose the worldly life and its adornment, the Messenger of God ﷺ would provide for them and divorce them, and that the separation does not occur merely by their choosing it without him effecting it. Most scholars said: This is the verse of choice (takhyir). So when he says to her, "Choose," and she chooses her husband, that is not a divorce. It is narrated from ʿAli that she becomes one revocable divorce even if she chooses herself. According to Abu Hanifah and his companions, which is also the view of ʿAli, one irrevocable divorce occurs if she chooses herself; according to al-Shafiʿi, it is one revocable divorce, which is also the view of ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿud; according to Malik, it is three. Most people held that the verse concerns choice and divorce, which is the view of ʿAli, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. The speaker of this view said: As for the matter of divorce, it is deferred. If they choose themselves, he considers how he will release them, and there is no offer of choice in divorce in it, because choice implies three pronouncements of divorce, and he has said: "and release you with a fair release," and there is no fair release with an absolute final divorce. End of quotation.

What the apparent meaning of the verse indicates is what we mentioned first: that He made the granting of provision and release from Him contingent upon their desire for the adornment of the worldly life. The meaning of the verse is that their greatest concern and aim was to indulge in this world and attain its bliss and adornment.

The discussion of ﴿fa-taʿālayna﴾ has already been covered in His saying: ﴿Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons﴾ [Al ʿImran: 61] in Al ʿImran.

﴿Umattiʿkunna﴾: It was said that providing (mutʿah) is obligatory in divorce; it was also said that it is recommended. The command in His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236] requires obligation according to the jurists' school, and the discussion of this and the detailed positions were covered in al-Baqarah. The fair release (tasrih jamil) is either a release without harm to the house, or fair praise, good belief, and good companionship if it is complete. The majority read ﴿umattiʿkunna﴾ with shaddah from matta; Zayd ibn ʿAli read it without shaddah from amtaʿa. The meaning of (aʿadda) is "prepared and facilitated." He used the apparent noun in place of the pronoun to draw attention to the attribute by which the great reward is merited for them, which is good-doing (ihsan), as if He said: "He prepared it for you," because whoever desires God, His Messenger, and the Last Abode is a doer of good. The reading of Humayd al-Kharraz: ﴿umattiʿkunna wa-usarriḥkunna﴾ with raf (damma) is an istiʾnaf (resumed new sentence); the majority read with jazm (sukun) as a response to the command, or as a response to the condition, and ﴿fa-taʿālayna﴾ would then be a parenthetical clause (jumlat iʿtirad) between the condition and its consequence, and the entry of the fa' upon a parenthetical clause does no harm. A similar example is the poet's saying:

"Know that the knowledge of a man benefits him: that everything decreed will certainly come."

Then He addressed the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, so that they would give attention to what they are addressed with, since it is a matter deserving attention. Zayd ibn ʿAli, (p-228) al-Jahdari, ʿAmr ibn Fa'id al-Aswari, and Yaʿqub read ﴿ta'ti﴾ with the feminine ta' (taʾnith), taking account of the meaning of man; the majority read it with the yaʾ, taking account of the wording of man.

﴿bi-fahishatin mubayyinah﴾: a grave sin among the sins. It should not be supposed that it is fornication, because of the infallibility of the Messenger of God ﷺ from that, and because He described it as clear, while fornication is something concealed. The indecency should rather be understood as disobedience to the husband and corruption of companionship. Since their dwelling was the place of descent of revelation of commands and prohibitions, this obligated them more because of that, and because they were under the Messenger ﷺ more than others would be, so their reward and punishment were doubled. Nafiʿ, Hamzah, ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read ﴿yudaʿaf﴾ with an alif and a fatha on the ʿayn; al-Hasan, ʿIsa, and Abu ʿAmr read it with shaddah and fatha on the ʿayn; al-Jahdari, Ibn Kathir, and Abu ʿAmir read it with nun and shaddah with kasrah on the ʿayn; Zayd ibn ʿAli, Ibn Muhaysin, and Kharijah from Abu ʿAmr read it with alif, nun, and kasrah; and a group read it with the yaʾ of the third person and alif and kasrah.
