It is related from Qatada: say, "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greater, and there is no power or might except through God." It is related from Mujahid: these words are said by the one in a state of purity and by the one in a state of major impurity (junub). ﴿بُكْرَةً وأصِيلًا﴾ (in the morning and the evening) requires "remember" and "glorify," and the accusative is governed by the second, by the method of operating (i'mal). The two times are a metaphor for all of time; mentioning the two extremes indicates comprehensiveness. Ibn ʿAbbas said: i.e., pray the dawn prayer and the night prayer. Al-Akhfash said: what is between ʿasr and ʿisha. Qatada said: the reference by these two times is to the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer. It is also permitted that the command to remember and to increase it is an increase of acts of obedience and devotion to acts of obedience, for every act of obedience and every good is part of remembrance. Then He singled out from this glorification (al-tasbih) "in the morning and the evening," which is the prayer at all its times, being superior to other prayers; or the dawn and night prayers, because performing them is more difficult.

When He commanded them to remember and glorify, He mentioned His goodness by His bestowing blessings upon them, He and His angels. Al-Hasan said: ﴿يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ (He sends blessings upon you) means: He has mercy on you. Ibn Jubayr said: He forgives you. Abu al-ʿAliya said: He praises you. It was also said: He is kind to you. The blessing of the angels is seeking forgiveness, as in His saying: ﴿ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ (and they seek forgiveness for those who believe) [Ghafir: 7]. Muqatil said: it is supplication; the meaning is: He is the One who has mercy upon you, in that He calls you to good and commands you to increase remembrance and obedience, so as to bring you out of the darknesses of disobedience into the light of obedience. Ibn Zayd said: from error to guidance. Muqatil said: from disbelief to faith. It was said: from the Fire to Paradise, related by al-Mawardi. It was said: from the graves to the resurrection. ﴿ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾ (and His angels) is coordinated with the pronoun in ﴿يُصَلِّي﴾ that is concealed (in it), and the separation by the prepositional phrase has dispensed with emphasis. The blessing of God is other than the blessing of the angels, so how do they share in a common measure? It is the will for good to reach them. God, by His mercy toward them, wills the delivery of good to them, and His angels by seeking forgiveness wish for that. Al-Zamakhshari said: they were made, because they are those whose supplication is answered, as if they are the ones performing mercy and compassion. A parallel is their saying: "May God give you life" (hayyaka Allah), meaning: may He give you life and preserve you; and "I give you life" (hayyaytuka), meaning: I supplicated for you that God give you life; because by relying on the answer to your supplication, it is as if you cause him to remain in reality; likewise, "God lengthen your life" (ʿammarakum Allah) and "I lengthen your life," "God give you drink" (saqaka Allah) and "I gave you drink." To this belongs His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ ومَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلى النَّبِيِّ ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ (Indeed God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him) [al-Ahzab: 56], i.e., supplicate for him that blessings be sent upon him.

﴿وكانَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا﴾ (and He is ever Merciful to the believers) is evidence that the intended meaning of "blessing" is mercy. End of quotation. What he mentioned, that it is "as if they are doing," includes combining the literal and the metaphorical; and what we mentioned, that the two blessings share a common measure, is more preferable.

﴿تَحِيَّتُهم يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ (their greeting on the day they meet Him) means: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ (peace) means: God's greeting to them. He says to the believers: "Peace be upon you, welcome, My servants who pleased Me by following My command," as al-Raqashi said. It was also said: the angels greet them with safety from every detestable thing. Al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib said: its meaning is that the angel of death does not seize the soul of the believer until he has greeted him with peace. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the angel of death comes to seize the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings." It was said: according to this, the pronoun in His saying ﴿يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ refers to something not mentioned. It was said: it is the greeting of the angels upon their emergence from the graves. Qatada said: on the day of their entering Paradise, some of them greet others with peace, meaning: we are safe and you are safe from every fearful thing. It was said: the angels greet them on that day. It was said: it is the greeting of the angel of death and the angels with him upon them, and their good news of Paradise. "Greeting" (tahiyya) is a verbal noun in these sayings, attributed to its object, except in the view of one who said it is a verbal noun attributed to the one greeting and the one greeted, not in the sense of operating; because a single pronoun cannot be both subject and object. Rather, it is like His saying: ﴿وكُنّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ﴾ (and We were witnesses to their judgment) [al-Anbiya: 78], i.e., for the judgment that took place among them. So this greeting that takes place between them is peace. Al-Mubarrad distinguished between "greeting" (tahiyya) and "peace" (salam), saying: "greeting" is when that is supplication, while "peace" is specific; and from it: ﴿ويُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وسَلامًا﴾ (and they will be met therein with greeting and peace) [al-Furqan: 75]. ﴿والأجْرُ الكَرِيمُ﴾ (and a noble reward) is Paradise.

﴿شاهِدًا﴾ (a witness) over those to whom you were sent, and over their denial and their affirmation; i.e., your saying is effective with God, and a witness to the conveyance to them, and to the conveyance of the prophets' sayings. ﴿شاهِدًا﴾ is in the accusative as a qualifier of a future state (hal muqaddara), if your saying with God at the time of sending was not yet a witness over them, but was to become a witness at the time of bearing witness and at its performance; or because it is the closest time to the sending, and the faith of those who believed and the denial of those who denied occurred within a single time.

﴿وداعِيًا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ (and as one who calls to God). Ibn ʿAbbas said: the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn ʿIsa said: to obedience. ﴿بِإذْنِهِ﴾ (by His permission) means: by His facilitation and easing, and it does not mean the literal permission; because it is understood from His saying "We have sent you as a caller" that he is permitted to call. Since calling the polytheist to monotheism was extremely difficult, it was said: "by His permission," i.e., by His facilitation, may He be exalted. ﴿وسِراجًا مُنِيرًا﴾ (and as a shining lamp) illuminates the darkness of polytheism, and by it the astray are guided, just as the darkness of night is illuminated by a shining lamp. And one is guided by it when God, through the light of his prophethood, increases the light of insight, just as He increases the light of sight through the light of the lamp. He described it as giving light, because some lamps do not give light when their oil is scant and their wick is thin. Al-Zajjaj said: it is coordinated with ﴿شاهِدًا﴾, i.e., "and one who has a shining lamp," i.e., a luminous book. Al-Farra' said: if you wish, it is in the accusative, meaning: "and reciting a shining lamp." Al-Zamakhshari said: according to this interpretation it may also be coordinated with the kaf in ﴿أرْسَلْناكَ﴾ (We have sent you). End of quotation. What he said is not clear, since the meaning becomes: "We sent one who is a shining lamp," which is the Qur'an; and the Qur'an is not described as being sent, but as being sent down. Likewise, if the estimate is "and reciting," the meaning becomes: "We sent a reciter of a shining lamp," which contains coordinating an attribute belonging to the essence onto the essence, like your saying: "I saw Zayd and the scholar," if "the scholar" is an attribute of Zayd; and coordination indicates difference, so such an analysis does not fittingly apply to the speech of God. Rather, it is interpreted according to what eloquence and rhetoric require.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that He sent His Prophet as a witness (shahidan), and so on to its end, this included the command to adopt those states. It is as if He said: "So bear witness, give good tidings, warn, invite, and forbid." Then He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ This is connected to what precedes it in meaning, although it appears to be disconnected from what came before it. Al-fadl al-kabir (the great bounty) means the reward, from their saying of gifts: fudul and fawadil, or it means an increase upon the reward. When the one bestowed with grace and its greatness is mentioned, what is your opinion of the reward, or of what they were favored with over the rest of the nations? That comes from Him, exalted is He, or it refers to the Garden and what they are given therein? It is explained by: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, in the meadows of the Gardens, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 22]

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ This is a prohibition to him, peace be upon him, from listening to them in matters they sought that are not obligatory, and in matters in which they offer him advice, which is deceit.

﴿And leave their harm.﴾ The apparent reading is that it is an idafa (construct) to the object. When He forbade obeying them, He commanded him to leave off harming and punishing them. From this, what concerns the disbelievers was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword. ﴿And rely upon Allah,﴾ for He will help you and forsake them. It is permissible that it be a verbal noun (masdar) in idafa to the agent, meaning: "leave their harming you," that is, the requiting of harm through punishment or otherwise, until you are commanded. This is the interpretation of Mujahid.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verse 36–48 (part 1 of 3):

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose. You feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no further need of her, We married her to you, so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no further need of them. And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾ ﴿There is no discomfort for the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. [This is] the way of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a decree decreed.﴾ ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ ﴿And exalt Him morning and evening.﴾ ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. And ever is He merciful to the believers.﴾ ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace," and He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner,﴾ ﴿And as one who invites to Allah by His permission and as a lamp giving light.﴾ ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾.

(p-233) The majority of scholars, Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, Mujahid and others said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed on behalf of Zayd the marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, but she refused and said, "I am not one to marry him." He said, "Yes, [you are]; so marry him, for I am pleased with him for you." She refused, and so this verse was revealed. It is mentioned that she and her brother ʿAbdullah disliked that, but when the verse was revealed, they were pleased. Ibn Zayd said: Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, who was the first woman to offer herself to the Prophet, gave herself to him, and he said, "I have accepted you and married you to Zayd ibn Harithah." She and her brother were displeased and said, "We only wanted him [the Prophet], yet he married us to his slave." So this verse was revealed. But the first cause is more sound. The connection of this verse is that when [Allah] mentioned those previous attributes of Islam and what follows, He followed that with what had proceeded from some of the Muslims, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicated a matter which some of them refused, and so they were rebuked, since obedience to him, peace be upon him, is obedience to Allah, and his command is His command.

Al-khiyarah (choice) is a verbal noun from takhayyara, contrary to the regular analogy, like al-tiyarah from tatayyara. It has also been read with a sukun on the ya, reported by ʿIsa ibn Sulayman. The two Harami readers, the two ʿIraqi readers (al-ʿArabiyyan), Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, al-Aʿraj and ʿIsa read "an takuna" with the feminine ta; (p-234) while the Kufans, al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash and al-Sulami read it with the ya. Since the phrase "li-mu'minin wa la mu'minah" is general in a negative context, the pronoun came plural according to meaning in His saying "lahum," giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine. Al-Zamakhshari said: The pronoun should have been singular, as you say: "ma ja'anee min rajulin wa la imra'atin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha" [No man or woman came to me but that it was of such a matter]. End. It is not as he mentioned, because this is a conjunction with waw, so it is not permissible to make the pronoun singular except by an implied ellipsis, i.e., "ma ja'anee min rajulin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha," and you say, "ma ja'a Zayd wa la ʿAmr illa darabā Khalidan" (neither Zayd nor ʿAmr came except that they struck Khalid); and it is not permissible to say "illa darab" except by ellipsis, as we have said.

﴿And when you said﴾ the address is to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

﴿to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ by Islam, which is the greatest blessing, and he is Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Messenger (ﷺ) had adopted.

﴿and you had bestowed favour on him﴾ which is his manumission; part of his story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ and she is Zaynab bint Jahsh; it has been mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) had proposed her for him. It has also been said: Allah bestowed favour on him by your companionship and affection, and you bestowed favour on him by adopting him. "Zayd came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to separate from my companion. He said: 'Has something in her troubled you?' He said: No, by Allah, but she is haughty towards me because of her nobility, and she hurts me with her tongue. He said: '﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾,' meaning: do not divorce her, and it is a command of recommendation, '﴿and fear Allah﴾ in treating her well.' So he divorced her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her after the completion of her waiting period." He gave as the reason for his marrying her His saying: ﴿so that there would be no discomfort for the believers﴾ in marrying the wives of those whom they had adopted when they separate from them, and that these wives are not included in what was forbidden in His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [an-Nisa 23].

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn said: Allah had revealed to him that Zayd would divorce her, and that he would marry her by Allah's marrying her to him. When Zayd complained of her character and that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wished to divorce her, he said to him, "﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾," by way of good manners and advice, while he knew that he would divorce her. This is what he concealed within himself, and he did not intend that he commanded him to divorce. When he knew that he would divorce her, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that a saying from the people would reach him about marrying Zaynab after Zayd, since he was his mawla, and he had commanded him to divorce her; so Allah rebuked him for this degree of [concern] in a matter which Allah had permitted, by saying "keep [your wife]" while knowing that he would divorce; so He informed him that Allah has more right to be feared, that is, in every situation. End. This report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn is what the researching commentators hold, such as al-Zuhri, Bakr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, al-Qushayri, the judge Abu Bakr ibn al-ʿArabi and others. What is meant by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾ is only the slander of the hypocrites concerning the marriage of the wives of the Prophets, and the Prophet is protected in his movements and stillnesses. Some commentators have remarks on this verse that imply a deficiency in the station of prophethood, which we pass over. It has also been said: His saying ﴿and fear Allah, while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose﴾ is an address from Allah, mighty and majestic, or from the Prophet (ﷺ) to Zayd, for he concealed his inclination towards her and displayed his aversion from her, when he thought that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended that she be among his wives. End.

Al-Zamakhshari has a lengthy discussion on this verse, and part of it is not fitting to mention, containing what is not correct, having followed the Mu'tazilite school and others; I have chosen from it what I quote. He said: How often a person guards against something and is ashamed for people to know about it, while in itself it is permissible, broad and absolutely lawful, with no blame and no fault before Allah. Entering into that permissible matter may be a ladder to attaining obligations, for the greatness of their effect in religion and the great reward; and if it were not guarded against, many people would loosen their tongues about it, except those who have been given virtue, knowledge, religion and insight into the realities and essence of things rather than their outward forms. Do you not see that when they hoped for the houses of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would remain sitting in their gatherings, not persisting in being at ease with conversation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was troubled by their sitting and his heart was constricted by their talk, while shyness prevented him from commanding them to disperse, until the revelation: ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 53]. Had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) revealed what was hidden in his heart and commanded them to disperse, it would have been difficult for them and would have caused some speech. So this is of that kind, for the inclination of a person's heart towards some of his desires, from a woman or otherwise, is not described as ugly by reason or by Sharia. Taking the permissible in the lawful manner is not ugly either, and that is the proposal for Zaynab and marrying her without pressuring Zayd or requesting from him. It was not considered objectionable among them that a man should relinquish his wife to his friend, nor disgraceful if he relinquished her that the other should marry her. For when the Emigrants entered Madinah, the Helpers preferred them with everything, so much so that a man among them who had two wives would relinquish one of them and give her in marriage to an Emigrant. When the matter is permissible in all its aspects, and there is no aspect of ugliness in it, nor corruption nor harm to Zayd or anyone, but rather it brings in benefits—to say nothing of one of them: that the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was secured from being left without a husband and from neglect, attained nobility, and became a mother among the mothers of the believers—along with the general benefit which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in His saying: ﴿so that there would be no [discomfort]﴾ the verse. End of what we have chosen from al-Zamakhshari's words. His saying ﴿amsik ʿalayka﴾ contains the connection of the raising verb to the attached pronoun to the genitive pronoun, while both refer to one person, so it is like His saying in the poem:

*Be at ease, and leave aside the plunder cried out over its enclosures.*

They mentioned concerning this construction that "ʿala" and "ʿan" are nouns and cannot be particles, because of the impossibility of "fakkara fika" and "aʿnee bika"; rather, this is one where the self is meant, i.e., "fakkir fi nafsika" (think within yourself) and "aʿnee bi-nafsika" (mean by yourself). We have discussed this in His saying: ﴿and shake towards you﴾ [Maryam 25] and ﴿and draw your wing towards you﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. Al-Hufi said: ﴿and you conceal within yourself﴾ is a resumed sentence, and ﴿and fear﴾ is conjoined to "and you conceal." Al-Zamakhshari said: it is the waw of circumstance, meaning: you say to Zayd, "﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾" while concealing within yourself the desire that he not keep her, and you conceal, fearing the people's talk; or it is the waw of conjunction, as if it were said: "and that you combine your saying 'keep' with concealing the talk and fearing the people." End. "And you conceal" cannot be a circumstantial clause with an implied subject, i.e., "while you conceal," because it is an affirmative present verb, so the waw does not enter it except under that implication, and that is itself rare and unusual, and rules are not built upon such; and from it is their saying: "I stood up while I strike his eye," i.e., "while I strike his eye."

﴿And Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ its parsing has been discussed in similar form in al-Tawbah.

﴿So when Zayd had no further need of her﴾ that is, [he had no] need, it is said: this is intercourse, as Ibn ʿAbbas said. Abu ʿIsmah Nuh ibn Abi Maryam narrated with a chain traced back to Zaynab that she said: "I was not refusing him, but Allah prevented me from him." It is also said: from the time he married her, he was not able to enjoy her; it was narrated that he would become swollen when he wanted to be intimate with her. Qatadah said: the *watar* here is divorce. The majority read "zawwajnakaha" with the plural of majesty; Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and his two brothers al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and their father ʿAli, read "zawwajtukaha" with the first-person singular pronoun. He, exalted is He, removed discomfort from the believers in treating the wives of adopted sons as the wives of prophets in their being forbidden to them after the ties of marriage between them had ended. ﴿And the command of Allah﴾ that is, the requirement of Allah's command, or what is implied in His command. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: otherwise the command is eternal and is not described as "made" (mafʿul); it is possible, though remotely, that "command" here means one of the matters whose nature is to be done. Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿And the command of Allah﴾ which He wills to be ﴿done﴾ (*maf'ulan*), a thing that will certainly exist, and it is an example of what He willed to come into being of the marriage of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Zaynab. It is also possible that "the command of Allah" means "the existent," since it is the object of "yakun" (to be). When He removed discomfort from the believers in what was mentioned, and the Messenger (ﷺ) was included among them, since he is the master of the believers, He removed discomfort from him specifically, as a mark of honour and dignity, and He removed discomfort from him twice: once by inclusion in the general, and once by specification.

﴿فِيما فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ﴾ (in what God had ordained for him). Al-Hasan said: in what was specific to him regarding the validity of marriage without a dowry (sadaq). Qatada said: in what He made lawful for him. Al-Dahhak said: in the allowance beyond four wives. The Jews had criticized him for marrying many times and having many wives, so God answered them with His words, ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ (the way of God), meaning: among the prophets, with many women, to the point that Sulayman, peace be upon him, had three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines, and Dawud had one hundred wives and three hundred concubines. It was also said that the reference is to the Messenger ﷺ having combined in his marriage Zaynab and others, just as Dawud combined the woman he married after her husband was killed. ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ is in the accusative either as a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun (masdar), as al-Zamakhshari said; or as a verbal noun itself; or by an understood verb whose estimate is "adhere to" or the like; or as an incitement (al-igra'), as if he had said: "upon him is the way of God." Ibn 'Atiyya said: his saying "or as an incitement" is not good, because the operator of the noun in an incitement may not be omitted; moreover, its estimate would be "upon him is the way of God" with a third-person pronoun, and that is not permitted in an incitement, since one does not incite an absent person. What came in their saying "upon him, a man who blames me" has an interpretation, and it is rare in any case. ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾ (those who passed away) refers to the prophets, as evidenced by their description after His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (who convey the messages of God). ﴿وكانَ أمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ (and the command of God is) means: His commands, and all existing things are from His command, so they are decreed. His saying ﴿قَدَرًا﴾ (a decree) means: possessing a measure, or according to a measure, or a decree decreed and a fixed judgment. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ (those who) is an attribute of ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾, or it is in the nominative, or in the accusative by an understood "them," or by "I praise." ʿAbd Allah read ﴿الَّذِينَ بَلَّغُوا﴾ (who conveyed) as a past verb. Ubayy read ﴿رِسالَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ (the message of God) in the singular; the majority read ﴿يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ﴾ in the plural. ﴿وكَفى بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا﴾ (and God suffices as a reckoner) means: a reckoner of all deeds and beliefs; or ḥasīb in the sense of "sufficient," i.e., adequate.

Then He negated that His Messenger was ﴿أبا أحَدٍ مِن رِجالِكُمْ﴾ (the father of any man among you), meaning that between him and the one he adopted there was no bond of in-law relationship or marriage such as exists between a father and his son. This is the aim of this clause; the aim is not that he had no son, so that he would need to argue about his sons by saying they had died, nor about al-Hasan and al-Husayn by saying they were infants. The attribution of ﴿رِجالِكم﴾ (your men) to the addressees' pronoun excludes his sons, because they are his men, not the men of the addressees. The majority read ﴿ولَكِنْ رَسُولَ﴾ (but the Messenger of) with the lightened ﴿لَكِنْ﴾ (but) and the accusative ﴿رَسُولَ﴾, by an ellipsis of "was" (kāna), indicated by the earlier "was"; it was said: or by coordination with ﴿أبا أحَدٍ﴾. ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read it with the emphatic ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾ (but indeed) and the accusative, as the predicate of ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾, the predicate being omitted, its estimate being: "but indeed the Messenger of God and the seal of the prophets is he," i.e., Muhammad. Omitting the predicate of ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾ and its sisters is permitted when there is an indication. Among what came in this is the poet's saying:

"Had you been a Dabbi, you would have known my kinship,
but [I am] a Zanji with huge lips."

I.e., you do not know my kinship. Zayd ibn ʿAli and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read it with the lightened ﴿لَكِنْ﴾ and the nominative ﴿ورَسُولُهُ﴾ and ﴿خاتَمُ﴾, meaning: but he is a messenger, as the poet said:

"I am not the eloquent poet among them,
but I am a bulwark of the spears of war."

I.e., but I am a bulwark. The majority read ﴿خاتِمَ﴾ (seal) with a kasra on the ta', meaning that he sealed them, i.e., came last of them. It is related from him that he said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets," and from him: "I am the seal of the prophets," in the hadith of "the brick." It is also related from him, peace be upon him, expressions that indicate explicitly that there is no prophet after him, and the meaning is that no one should claim prophethood after him. The descent of ʿIsa at the end of time does not contradict this, because he is among those who were prophets before him, and he will descend acting according to the law of Muhammad, facing his qibla, as if he were one of his community. Ibn ʿAtiyya said: what al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib mentioned in his book called al-Hidaya, about allowing a possibility in the words of this verse, is weak; and what al-Ghazali mentioned about this verse and this meaning in his book called al-Iqtisad, and touched upon to avoid confusing the belief of the Muslims regarding the sealing of prophethood by Muhammad, must be guarded against; so beware, beware of it, and God guides by His mercy. Al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Zayd ibn ʿAli, al-Aʿraj (with a variant), and ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the ta', meaning: they were sealed by him, so he is like the seal and the stamp for them.

Whoever holds that prophethood is acquired and does not end, or that the saint (wali) is superior to the prophet, is a heretic (zindiq) who must be killed. Some have claimed prophethood, and the Muslims killed them for that. In our own age there was a man of the poor who claimed prophethood in the city of Malaga, and the sultan Ibn al-Ahmar, king of al-Andalus at Granada, killed him and crucified him until his flesh scattered.

﴿وكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾ (and God is ever Knowing of all things). This is general, and the intended meaning here is His knowledge of what He saw as best for His Messenger, and of what He decreed in the whole matter. Then He commanded the believers to remember Him by praising Him, glorifying Him, sanctifying Him, and exalting Him above what is not fitting for Him. "Much remembrance" (al-dhikr al-kathir): Ibn ʿAbbas said: that one never forgets Him ever; or glorification (tasbih) is included in remembrance, but it was singled out because it exalts Him, may He be exalted, above what is not fitting for Him, so it is the best of remembrances or among the best of them. It is related from Qatada: say, "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greater, and there is no power or might except through God." It is related from Mujahid: these words are said by the one in a state of purity and by the one in a state of major impurity (junub). ﴿بُكْرَةً وأصِيلًا﴾ (in the morning and the evening) requires "remember" and "glorify," and the accusative is governed by the second, by the method of operating (i'mal). The two times are a metaphor for all of time; mentioning the two extremes indicates comprehensiveness. Ibn ʿAbbas said: i.e., pray the dawn prayer and the night prayer. Al-Akhfash said: what is between ʿasr and ʿisha. Qatada said: the reference by these two times is to the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer. It is also permitted that the command to remember and to increase it is an increase of acts of obedience and devotion to acts of obedience, for every act of obedience and every good is part of remembrance. Then He singled out from this glorification (al-tasbih) "in the morning and the evening," which is the prayer at all its times, being superior to other prayers; or the dawn and night prayers, because performing them is more difficult.

When He commanded them to remember and glorify, He mentioned His goodness by His bestowing blessings upon them, He and His angels. Al-Hasan said: ﴿يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ (He sends blessings upon you) means: He has mercy on you. Ibn Jubayr said: He forgives you. Abu al-ʿAliya said: He praises you. It was also said: He is kind to you. The blessing of the angels is seeking forgiveness, as in His saying: ﴿ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ (and they seek forgiveness for those who believe) [Ghafir: 7]. Muqatil said: it is supplication; the meaning is: He is the One who has mercy upon you, in that He calls you to good and commands you to increase remembrance and obedience, so as to bring you out of the darknesses of disobedience into the light of obedience. Ibn Zayd said: from error to guidance. Muqatil said: from disbelief to faith. It was said: from the Fire to Paradise, related by al-Mawardi. It was said: from the graves to the resurrection. ﴿ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾ (and His angels) is coordinated with the pronoun in ﴿يُصَلِّي﴾ that is concealed (in it), and the separation by the prepositional phrase has dispensed with emphasis. The blessing of God is other than the blessing of the angels, so how do they share in a common measure? It is the will for good to reach them. God, by His mercy toward them, wills the delivery of good to them, and His angels by seeking forgiveness wish for that. Al-Zamakhshari said: they were made, because they are those whose supplication is answered, as if they are the ones performing mercy and compassion. A parallel is their saying: "May God give you life" (hayyaka Allah), meaning: may He give you life and preserve you; and "I give you life" (hayyaytuka), meaning: I supplicated for you that God give you life; because by relying on the answer to your supplication, it is as if you cause him to remain in reality; likewise, "God lengthen your life" (ʿammarakum Allah) and "I lengthen your life," "God give you drink" (saqaka Allah) and "I gave you drink." To this belongs His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ ومَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلى النَّبِيِّ ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ (Indeed God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him) [al-Ahzab: 56], i.e., supplicate for him that blessings be sent upon him.

﴿وكانَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا﴾ (and He is ever Merciful to the believers) is evidence that the intended meaning of "blessing" is mercy. End of quotation. What he mentioned, that it is "as if they are doing," includes combining the literal and the metaphorical; and what we mentioned, that the two blessings share a common measure, is more preferable.

﴿تَحِيَّتُهم يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ (their greeting on the day they meet Him) means: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ (peace) means: God's greeting to them. He says to the believers: "Peace be upon you, welcome, My servants who pleased Me by following My command," as al-Raqashi said. It was also said: the angels greet them with safety from every detestable thing. Al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib said: its meaning is that the angel of death does not seize the soul of the believer until he has greeted him with peace. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the angel of death comes to seize the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings." It was said: according to this, the pronoun in His saying ﴿يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ refers to something not mentioned. It was said: it is the greeting of the angels upon their emergence from the graves. Qatada said: on the day of their entering Paradise, some of them greet others with peace, meaning: we are safe and you are safe from every fearful thing. It was said: the angels greet them on that day. It was said: it is the greeting of the angel of death and the angels with him upon them, and their good news of Paradise. "Greeting" (tahiyya) is a verbal noun in these sayings, attributed to its object, except in the view of one who said it is a verbal noun attributed to the one greeting and the one greeted, not in the sense of operating; because a single pronoun cannot be both subject and object. Rather, it is like His saying: ﴿وكُنّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ﴾ (and We were witnesses to their judgment) [al-Anbiya: 78], i.e., for the judgment that took place among them. So this greeting that takes place between them is peace. Al-Mubarrad distinguished between "greeting" (tahiyya) and "peace" (salam), saying: "greeting" is when that is supplication, while "peace" is specific; and from it: ﴿ويُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وسَلامًا﴾ (and they will be met therein with greeting and peace) [al-Furqan: 75]. ﴿والأجْرُ الكَرِيمُ﴾ (and a noble reward) is Paradise.

﴿شاهِدًا﴾ (a witness) over those to whom you were sent, and over their denial and their affirmation; i.e., your saying is effective with God, and a witness to the conveyance to them, and to the conveyance of the prophets' sayings. ﴿شاهِدًا﴾ is in the accusative as a qualifier of a future state (hal muqaddara), if your saying with God at the time of sending was not yet a witness over them, but was to become a witness at the time of bearing witness and at its performance; or because it is the closest time to the sending, and the faith of those who believed and the denial of those who denied occurred within a single time.

﴿وداعِيًا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ (and as one who calls to God). Ibn ʿAbbas said: the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn ʿIsa said: to obedience. ﴿بِإذْنِهِ﴾ (by His permission) means: by His facilitation and easing, and it does not mean the literal permission; because it is understood from His saying "We have sent you as a caller" that he is permitted to call. Since calling the polytheist to monotheism was extremely difficult, it was said: "by His permission," i.e., by His facilitation, may He be exalted. ﴿وسِراجًا مُنِيرًا﴾ (and as a shining lamp) illuminates the darkness of polytheism, and by it the astray are guided, just as the darkness of night is illuminated by a shining lamp. And one is guided by it when God, through the light of his prophethood, increases the light of insight, just as He increases the light of sight through the light of the lamp. He described it as giving light, because some lamps do not give light when their oil is scant and their wick is thin. Al-Zajjaj said: it is coordinated with ﴿شاهِدًا﴾, i.e., "and one who has a shining lamp," i.e., a luminous book. Al-Farra' said: if you wish, it is in the accusative, meaning: "and reciting a shining lamp." Al-Zamakhshari said: according to this interpretation it may also be coordinated with the kaf in ﴿أرْسَلْناكَ﴾ (We have sent you). End of quotation. What he said is not clear, since the meaning becomes: "We sent one who is a shining lamp," which is the Qur'an; and the Qur'an is not described as being sent, but as being sent down. Likewise, if the estimate is "and reciting," the meaning becomes: "We sent a reciter of a shining lamp," which contains coordinating an attribute belonging to the essence onto the essence, like your saying: "I saw Zayd and the scholar," if "the scholar" is an attribute of Zayd; and coordination indicates difference, so such an analysis does not fittingly apply to the speech of God. Rather, it is interpreted according to what eloquence and rhetoric require.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that He sent His Prophet as a witness (shahidan), and so on to its end, this included the command to adopt those states. It is as if He said: "So bear witness, give good tidings, warn, invite, and forbid." Then He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ This is connected to what precedes it in meaning, although it appears to be disconnected from what came before it. Al-fadl al-kabir (the great bounty) means the reward, from their saying of gifts: fudul and fawadil, or it means an increase upon the reward. When the one bestowed with grace and its greatness is mentioned, what is your opinion of the reward, or of what they were favored with over the rest of the nations? That comes from Him, exalted is He, or it refers to the Garden and what they are given therein? It is explained by: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, in the meadows of the Gardens, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 22]

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ This is a prohibition to him, peace be upon him, from listening to them in matters they sought that are not obligatory, and in matters in which they offer him advice, which is deceit.

﴿And leave their harm.﴾ The apparent reading is that it is an idafa (construct) to the object. When He forbade obeying them, He commanded him to leave off harming and punishing them. From this, what concerns the disbelievers was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword. ﴿And rely upon Allah,﴾ for He will help you and forsake them. It is permissible that it be a verbal noun (masdar) in idafa to the agent, meaning: "leave their harming you," that is, the requiting of harm through punishment or otherwise, until you are commanded. This is the interpretation of Mujahid.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verse 36–48 (part 1 of 3):

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose. You feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no further need of her, We married her to you, so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no further need of them. And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾ ﴿There is no discomfort for the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. [This is] the way of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a decree decreed.﴾ ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ ﴿And exalt Him morning and evening.﴾ ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. And ever is He merciful to the believers.﴾ ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace," and He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner,﴾ ﴿And as one who invites to Allah by His permission and as a lamp giving light.﴾ ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾.

(p-233) The majority of scholars, Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, Mujahid and others said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed on behalf of Zayd the marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, but she refused and said, "I am not one to marry him." He said, "Yes, [you are]; so marry him, for I am pleased with him for you." She refused, and so this verse was revealed. It is mentioned that she and her brother ʿAbdullah disliked that, but when the verse was revealed, they were pleased. Ibn Zayd said: Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, who was the first woman to offer herself to the Prophet, gave herself to him, and he said, "I have accepted you and married you to Zayd ibn Harithah." She and her brother were displeased and said, "We only wanted him [the Prophet], yet he married us to his slave." So this verse was revealed. But the first cause is more sound. The connection of this verse is that when [Allah] mentioned those previous attributes of Islam and what follows, He followed that with what had proceeded from some of the Muslims, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicated a matter which some of them refused, and so they were rebuked, since obedience to him, peace be upon him, is obedience to Allah, and his command is His command.

Al-khiyarah (choice) is a verbal noun from takhayyara, contrary to the regular analogy, like al-tiyarah from tatayyara. It has also been read with a sukun on the ya, reported by ʿIsa ibn Sulayman. The two Harami readers, the two ʿIraqi readers (al-ʿArabiyyan), Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, al-Aʿraj and ʿIsa read "an takuna" with the feminine ta; (p-234) while the Kufans, al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash and al-Sulami read it with the ya. Since the phrase "li-mu'minin wa la mu'minah" is general in a negative context, the pronoun came plural according to meaning in His saying "lahum," giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine. Al-Zamakhshari said: The pronoun should have been singular, as you say: "ma ja'anee min rajulin wa la imra'atin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha" [No man or woman came to me but that it was of such a matter]. End. It is not as he mentioned, because this is a conjunction with waw, so it is not permissible to make the pronoun singular except by an implied ellipsis, i.e., "ma ja'anee min rajulin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha," and you say, "ma ja'a Zayd wa la ʿAmr illa darabā Khalidan" (neither Zayd nor ʿAmr came except that they struck Khalid); and it is not permissible to say "illa darab" except by ellipsis, as we have said.

﴿And when you said﴾ the address is to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

﴿to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ by Islam, which is the greatest blessing, and he is Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Messenger (ﷺ) had adopted.

﴿and you had bestowed favour on him﴾ which is his manumission; part of his story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ and she is Zaynab bint Jahsh; it has been mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) had proposed her for him. It has also been said: Allah bestowed favour on him by your companionship and affection, and you bestowed favour on him by adopting him. "Zayd came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to separate from my companion. He said: 'Has something in her troubled you?' He said: No, by Allah, but she is haughty towards me because of her nobility, and she hurts me with her tongue. He said: '﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾,' meaning: do not divorce her, and it is a command of recommendation, '﴿and fear Allah﴾ in treating her well.' So he divorced her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her after the completion of her waiting period." He gave as the reason for his marrying her His saying: ﴿so that there would be no discomfort for the believers﴾ in marrying the wives of those whom they had adopted when they separate from them, and that these wives are not included in what was forbidden in His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [an-Nisa 23].

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn said: Allah had revealed to him that Zayd would divorce her, and that he would marry her by Allah's marrying her to him. When Zayd complained of her character and that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wished to divorce her, he said to him, "﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾," by way of good manners and advice, while he knew that he would divorce her. This is what he concealed within himself, and he did not intend that he commanded him to divorce. When he knew that he would divorce her, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that a saying from the people would reach him about marrying Zaynab after Zayd, since he was his mawla, and he had commanded him to divorce her; so Allah rebuked him for this degree of [concern] in a matter which Allah had permitted, by saying "keep [your wife]" while knowing that he would divorce; so He informed him that Allah has more right to be feared, that is, in every situation. End. This report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn is what the researching commentators hold, such as al-Zuhri, Bakr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, al-Qushayri, the judge Abu Bakr ibn al-ʿArabi and others. What is meant by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾ is only the slander of the hypocrites concerning the marriage of the wives of the Prophets, and the Prophet is protected in his movements and stillnesses. Some commentators have remarks on this verse that imply a deficiency in the station of prophethood, which we pass over. It has also been said: His saying ﴿and fear Allah, while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose﴾ is an address from Allah, mighty and majestic, or from the Prophet (ﷺ) to Zayd, for he concealed his inclination towards her and displayed his aversion from her, when he thought that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended that she be among his wives. End.

Al-Zamakhshari has a lengthy discussion on this verse, and part of it is not fitting to mention, containing what is not correct, having followed the Mu'tazilite school and others; I have chosen from it what I quote. He said: How often a person guards against something and is ashamed for people to know about it, while in itself it is permissible, broad and absolutely lawful, with no blame and no fault before Allah. Entering into that permissible matter may be a ladder to attaining obligations, for the greatness of their effect in religion and the great reward; and if it were not guarded against, many people would loosen their tongues about it, except those who have been given virtue, knowledge, religion and insight into the realities and essence of things rather than their outward forms. Do you not see that when they hoped for the houses of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would remain sitting in their gatherings, not persisting in being at ease with conversation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was troubled by their sitting and his heart was constricted by their talk, while shyness prevented him from commanding them to disperse, until the revelation: ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾ [al-Ahzab 53]. Had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) revealed what was hidden in his heart and commanded them to disperse, it would have been difficult for them and would have caused some speech. So this is of that kind, for the inclination of a person's heart towards some of his desires, from a woman or otherwise, is not described as ugly by reason or by Sharia. Taking the permissible in the lawful manner is not ugly either, and that is the proposal for Zaynab and marrying her without pressuring Zayd or requesting from him. It was not considered objectionable among them that a man should relinquish his wife to his friend, nor disgraceful if he relinquished her that the other should marry her. For when the Emigrants entered Madinah, the Helpers preferred them with everything, so much so that a man among them who had two wives would relinquish one of them and give her in marriage to an Emigrant. When the matter is permissible in all its aspects, and there is no aspect of ugliness in it, nor corruption nor harm to Zayd or anyone, but rather it brings in benefits—to say nothing of one of them: that the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was secured from being left without a husband and from neglect, attained nobility, and became a mother among the mothers of the believers—along with the general benefit which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned in His saying: ﴿so that there would be no [discomfort]﴾ the verse. End of what we have chosen from al-Zamakhshari's words. His saying ﴿amsik ʿalayka﴾ contains the connection of the raising verb to the attached pronoun to the genitive pronoun, while both refer to one person, so it is like His saying in the poem:

*Be at ease, and leave aside the plunder cried out over its enclosures.*

They mentioned concerning this construction that "ʿala" and "ʿan" are nouns and cannot be particles, because of the impossibility of "fakkara fika" and "aʿnee bika"; rather, this is one where the self is meant, i.e., "fakkir fi nafsika" (think within yourself) and "aʿnee bi-nafsika" (mean by yourself). We have discussed this in His saying: ﴿and shake towards you﴾ [Maryam 25] and ﴿and draw your wing towards you﴾ [al-Qasas 32]. Al-Hufi said: ﴿and you conceal within yourself﴾ is a resumed sentence, and ﴿and fear﴾ is conjoined to "and you conceal." Al-Zamakhshari said: it is the waw of circumstance, meaning: you say to Zayd, "﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾" while concealing within yourself the desire that he not keep her, and you conceal, fearing the people's talk; or it is the waw of conjunction, as if it were said: "and that you combine your saying 'keep' with concealing the talk and fearing the people." End. "And you conceal" cannot be a circumstantial clause with an implied subject, i.e., "while you conceal," because it is an affirmative present verb, so the waw does not enter it except under that implication, and that is itself rare and unusual, and rules are not built upon such; and from it is their saying: "I stood up while I strike his eye," i.e., "while I strike his eye."

﴿And Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ its parsing has been discussed in similar form in al-Tawbah.

﴿So when Zayd had no further need of her﴾ that is, [he had no] need, it is said: this is intercourse, as Ibn ʿAbbas said. Abu ʿIsmah Nuh ibn Abi Maryam narrated with a chain traced back to Zaynab that she said: "I was not refusing him, but Allah prevented me from him." It is also said: from the time he married her, he was not able to enjoy her; it was narrated that he would become swollen when he wanted to be intimate with her. Qatadah said: the *watar* here is divorce. The majority read "zawwajnakaha" with the plural of majesty; Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and his two brothers al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and their father ʿAli, read "zawwajtukaha" with the first-person singular pronoun. He, exalted is He, removed discomfort from the believers in treating the wives of adopted sons as the wives of prophets in their being forbidden to them after the ties of marriage between them had ended. ﴿And the command of Allah﴾ that is, the requirement of Allah's command, or what is implied in His command. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: otherwise the command is eternal and is not described as "made" (mafʿul); it is possible, though remotely, that "command" here means one of the matters whose nature is to be done. Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿And the command of Allah﴾ which He wills to be ﴿done﴾ (*maf'ulan*), a thing that will certainly exist, and it is an example of what He willed to come into being of the marriage of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Zaynab. It is also possible that "the command of Allah" means "the existent," since it is the object of "yakun" (to be). When He removed discomfort from the believers in what was mentioned, and the Messenger (ﷺ) was included among them, since he is the master of the believers, He removed discomfort from him specifically, as a mark of honour and dignity, and He removed discomfort from him twice: once by inclusion in the general, and once by specification.

﴿فِيما فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ﴾ (in what God had ordained for him). Al-Hasan said: in what was specific to him regarding the validity of marriage without a dowry (sadaq). Qatada said: in what He made lawful for him. Al-Dahhak said: in the allowance beyond four wives. The Jews had criticized him for marrying many times and having many wives, so God answered them with His words, ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ (the way of God), meaning: among the prophets, with many women, to the point that Sulayman, peace be upon him, had three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines, and Dawud had one hundred wives and three hundred concubines. It was also said that the reference is to the Messenger ﷺ having combined in his marriage Zaynab and others, just as Dawud combined the woman he married after her husband was killed. ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ is in the accusative either as a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun (masdar), as al-Zamakhshari said; or as a verbal noun itself; or by an understood verb whose estimate is "adhere to" or the like; or as an incitement (al-igra'), as if he had said: "upon him is the way of God." Ibn 'Atiyya said: his saying "or as an incitement" is not good, because the operator of the noun in an incitement may not be omitted; moreover, its estimate would be "upon him is the way of God" with a third-person pronoun, and that is not permitted in an incitement, since one does not incite an absent person. What came in their saying "upon him, a man who blames me" has an interpretation, and it is rare in any case. ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾ (those who passed away) refers to the prophets, as evidenced by their description after His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (who convey the messages of God). ﴿وكانَ أمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ (and the command of God is) means: His commands, and all existing things are from His command, so they are decreed. His saying ﴿قَدَرًا﴾ (a decree) means: possessing a measure, or according to a measure, or a decree decreed and a fixed judgment. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ (those who) is an attribute of ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا﴾, or it is in the nominative, or in the accusative by an understood "them," or by "I praise." ʿAbd Allah read ﴿الَّذِينَ بَلَّغُوا﴾ (who conveyed) as a past verb. Ubayy read ﴿رِسالَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ (the message of God) in the singular; the majority read ﴿يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ﴾ in the plural. ﴿وكَفى بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا﴾ (and God suffices as a reckoner) means: a reckoner of all deeds and beliefs; or ḥasīb in the sense of "sufficient," i.e., adequate.

Then He negated that His Messenger was ﴿أبا أحَدٍ مِن رِجالِكُمْ﴾ (the father of any man among you), meaning that between him and the one he adopted there was no bond of in-law relationship or marriage such as exists between a father and his son. This is the aim of this clause; the aim is not that he had no son, so that he would need to argue about his sons by saying they had died, nor about al-Hasan and al-Husayn by saying they were infants. The attribution of ﴿رِجالِكم﴾ (your men) to the addressees' pronoun excludes his sons, because they are his men, not the men of the addressees. The majority read ﴿ولَكِنْ رَسُولَ﴾ (but the Messenger of) with the lightened ﴿لَكِنْ﴾ (but) and the accusative ﴿رَسُولَ﴾, by an ellipsis of "was" (kāna), indicated by the earlier "was"; it was said: or by coordination with ﴿أبا أحَدٍ﴾. ʿAbd al-Warith, from Abu ʿAmr, read it with the emphatic ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾ (but indeed) and the accusative, as the predicate of ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾, the predicate being omitted, its estimate being: "but indeed the Messenger of God and the seal of the prophets is he," i.e., Muhammad. Omitting the predicate of ﴿لَكِنَّ﴾ and its sisters is permitted when there is an indication. Among what came in this is the poet's saying:

"Had you been a Dabbi, you would have known my kinship,
but [I am] a Zanji with huge lips."

I.e., you do not know my kinship. Zayd ibn ʿAli and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read it with the lightened ﴿لَكِنْ﴾ and the nominative ﴿ورَسُولُهُ﴾ and ﴿خاتَمُ﴾, meaning: but he is a messenger, as the poet said:

"I am not the eloquent poet among them,
but I am a bulwark of the spears of war."

I.e., but I am a bulwark. The majority read ﴿خاتِمَ﴾ (seal) with a kasra on the ta', meaning that he sealed them, i.e., came last of them. It is related from him that he said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets," and from him: "I am the seal of the prophets," in the hadith of "the brick." It is also related from him, peace be upon him, expressions that indicate explicitly that there is no prophet after him, and the meaning is that no one should claim prophethood after him. The descent of ʿIsa at the end of time does not contradict this, because he is among those who were prophets before him, and he will descend acting according to the law of Muhammad, facing his qibla, as if he were one of his community. Ibn ʿAtiyya said: what al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib mentioned in his book called al-Hidaya, about allowing a possibility in the words of this verse, is weak; and what al-Ghazali mentioned about this verse and this meaning in his book called al-Iqtisad, and touched upon to avoid confusing the belief of the Muslims regarding the sealing of prophethood by Muhammad, must be guarded against; so beware, beware of it, and God guides by His mercy. Al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Zayd ibn ʿAli, al-Aʿraj (with a variant), and ʿAsim read it with a fatha on the ta', meaning: they were sealed by him, so he is like the seal and the stamp for them.

Whoever holds that prophethood is acquired and does not end, or that the saint (wali) is superior to the prophet, is a heretic (zindiq) who must be killed. Some have claimed prophethood, and the Muslims killed them for that. In our own age there was a man of the poor who claimed prophethood in the city of Malaga, and the sultan Ibn al-Ahmar, king of al-Andalus at Granada, killed him and crucified him until his flesh scattered.

﴿وكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾ (and God is ever Knowing of all things). This is general, and the intended meaning here is His knowledge of what He saw as best for His Messenger, and of what He decreed in the whole matter. Then He commanded the believers to remember Him by praising Him, glorifying Him, sanctifying Him, and exalting Him above what is not fitting for Him. "Much remembrance" (al-dhikr al-kathir): Ibn ʿAbbas said: that one never forgets Him ever; or glorification (tasbih) is included in remembrance, but it was singled out because it exalts Him, may He be exalted, above what is not fitting for Him, so it is the best of remembrances or among the best of them. It is related from Qatada: say, "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greater, and there is no power or might except through God." It is related from Mujahid: these words are said by the one in a state of purity and by the one in a state of major impurity (junub). ﴿بُكْرَةً وأصِيلًا﴾ (in the morning and the evening) requires "remember" and "glorify," and the accusative is governed by the second, by the method of operating (i'mal). The two times are a metaphor for all of time; mentioning the two extremes indicates comprehensiveness. Ibn ʿAbbas said: i.e., pray the dawn prayer and the night prayer. Al-Akhfash said: what is between ʿasr and ʿisha. Qatada said: the reference by these two times is to the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer. It is also permitted that the command to remember and to increase it is an increase of acts of obedience and devotion to acts of obedience, for every act of obedience and every good is part of remembrance. Then He singled out from this glorification (al-tasbih) "in the morning and the evening," which is the prayer at all its times, being superior to other prayers; or the dawn and night prayers, because performing them is more difficult.

When He commanded them to remember and glorify, He mentioned His goodness by His bestowing blessings upon them, He and His angels. Al-Hasan said: ﴿يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ (He sends blessings upon you) means: He has mercy on you. Ibn Jubayr said: He forgives you. Abu al-ʿAliya said: He praises you. It was also said: He is kind to you. The blessing of the angels is seeking forgiveness, as in His saying: ﴿ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ (and they seek forgiveness for those who believe) [Ghafir: 7]. Muqatil said: it is supplication; the meaning is: He is the One who has mercy upon you, in that He calls you to good and commands you to increase remembrance and obedience, so as to bring you out of the darknesses of disobedience into the light of obedience. Ibn Zayd said: from error to guidance. Muqatil said: from disbelief to faith. It was said: from the Fire to Paradise, related by al-Mawardi. It was said: from the graves to the resurrection. ﴿ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾ (and His angels) is coordinated with the pronoun in ﴿يُصَلِّي﴾ that is concealed (in it), and the separation by the prepositional phrase has dispensed with emphasis. The blessing of God is other than the blessing of the angels, so how do they share in a common measure? It is the will for good to reach them. God, by His mercy toward them, wills the delivery of good to them, and His angels by seeking forgiveness wish for that. Al-Zamakhshari said: they were made, because they are those whose supplication is answered, as if they are the ones performing mercy and compassion. A parallel is their saying: "May God give you life" (hayyaka Allah), meaning: may He give you life and preserve you; and "I give you life" (hayyaytuka), meaning: I supplicated for you that God give you life; because by relying on the answer to your supplication, it is as if you cause him to remain in reality; likewise, "God lengthen your life" (ʿammarakum Allah) and "I lengthen your life," "God give you drink" (saqaka Allah) and "I gave you drink." To this belongs His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ ومَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلى النَّبِيِّ ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ﴾ (Indeed God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him) [al-Ahzab: 56], i.e., supplicate for him that blessings be sent upon him.

﴿وكانَ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا﴾ (and He is ever Merciful to the believers) is evidence that the intended meaning of "blessing" is mercy. End of quotation. What he mentioned, that it is "as if they are doing," includes combining the literal and the metaphorical; and what we mentioned, that the two blessings share a common measure, is more preferable.

﴿تَحِيَّتُهم يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ (their greeting on the day they meet Him) means: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ (peace) means: God's greeting to them. He says to the believers: "Peace be upon you, welcome, My servants who pleased Me by following My command," as al-Raqashi said. It was also said: the angels greet them with safety from every detestable thing. Al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib said: its meaning is that the angel of death does not seize the soul of the believer until he has greeted him with peace. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the angel of death comes to seize the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings." It was said: according to this, the pronoun in His saying ﴿يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ refers to something not mentioned. It was said: it is the greeting of the angels upon their emergence from the graves. Qatada said: on the day of their entering Paradise, some of them greet others with peace, meaning: we are safe and you are safe from every fearful thing. It was said: the angels greet them on that day. It was said: it is the greeting of the angel of death and the angels with him upon them, and their good news of Paradise. "Greeting" (tahiyya) is a verbal noun in these sayings, attributed to its object, except in the view of one who said it is a verbal noun attributed to the one greeting and the one greeted, not in the sense of operating; because a single pronoun cannot be both subject and object. Rather, it is like His saying: ﴿وكُنّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ﴾ (and We were witnesses to their judgment) [al-Anbiya: 78], i.e., for the judgment that took place among them. So this greeting that takes place between them is peace. Al-Mubarrad distinguished between "greeting" (tahiyya) and "peace" (salam), saying: "greeting" is when that is supplication, while "peace" is specific; and from it: ﴿ويُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وسَلامًا﴾ (and they will be met therein with greeting and peace) [al-Furqan: 75]. ﴿والأجْرُ الكَرِيمُ﴾ (and a noble reward) is Paradise.

﴿شاهِدًا﴾ (a witness) over those to whom you were sent, and over their denial and their affirmation; i.e., your saying is effective with God, and a witness to the conveyance to them, and to the conveyance of the prophets' sayings. ﴿شاهِدًا﴾ is in the accusative as a qualifier of a future state (hal muqaddara), if your saying with God at the time of sending was not yet a witness over them, but was to become a witness at the time of bearing witness and at its performance; or because it is the closest time to the sending, and the faith of those who believed and the denial of those who denied occurred within a single time.

﴿وداعِيًا إلى اللَّهِ﴾ (and as one who calls to God). Ibn ʿAbbas said: the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn ʿIsa said: to obedience. ﴿بِإذْنِهِ﴾ (by His permission) means: by His facilitation and easing, and it does not mean the literal permission; because it is understood from His saying "We have sent you as a caller" that he is permitted to call. Since calling the polytheist to monotheism was extremely difficult, it was said: "by His permission," i.e., by His facilitation, may He be exalted. ﴿وسِراجًا مُنِيرًا﴾ (and as a shining lamp) illuminates the darkness of polytheism, and by it the astray are guided, just as the darkness of night is illuminated by a shining lamp. And one is guided by it when God, through the light of his prophethood, increases the light of insight, just as He increases the light of sight through the light of the lamp. He described it as giving light, because some lamps do not give light when their oil is scant and their wick is thin. Al-Zajjaj said: it is coordinated with ﴿شاهِدًا﴾, i.e., "and one who has a shining lamp," i.e., a luminous book. Al-Farra' said: if you wish, it is in the accusative, meaning: "and reciting a shining lamp." Al-Zamakhshari said: according to this interpretation it may also be coordinated with the kaf in ﴿أرْسَلْناكَ﴾ (We have sent you). End of quotation. What he said is not clear, since the meaning becomes: "We sent one who is a shining lamp," which is the Qur'an; and the Qur'an is not described as being sent, but as being sent down. Likewise, if the estimate is "and reciting," the meaning becomes: "We sent a reciter of a shining lamp," which contains coordinating an attribute belonging to the essence onto the essence, like your saying: "I saw Zayd and the scholar," if "the scholar" is an attribute of Zayd; and coordination indicates difference, so such an analysis does not fittingly apply to the speech of God. Rather, it is interpreted according to what eloquence and rhetoric require.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that He sent His Prophet as a witness (shahidan), and so on to its end, this included the command to adopt those states. It is as if He said: "So bear witness, give good tidings, warn, invite, and forbid." Then He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ This is connected to what precedes it in meaning, although it appears to be disconnected from what came before it. Al-fadl al-kabir (the great bounty) means the reward, from their saying of gifts: fudul and fawadil, or it means an increase upon the reward. When the one bestowed with grace and its greatness is mentioned, what is your opinion of the reward, or of what they were favored with over the rest of the nations? That comes from Him, exalted is He, or it refers to the Garden and what they are given therein? It is explained by: ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, in the meadows of the Gardens, for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 22]

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.﴾ This is a prohibition to him, peace be upon him, from listening to them in matters they sought that are not obligatory, and in matters in which they offer him advice, which is deceit.

﴿And leave their harm.﴾ The apparent reading is that it is an idafa (construct) to the object. When He forbade obeying them, He commanded him to leave off harming and punishing them. From this, what concerns the disbelievers was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword. ﴿And rely upon Allah,﴾ for He will help you and forsake them. It is permissible that it be a verbal noun (masdar) in idafa to the agent, meaning: "leave their harming you," that is, the requiting of harm through punishment or otherwise, until you are commanded. This is the interpretation of Mujahid.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 33, verse 36–48 (part 1 of 3):

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose. You feared the people, but Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no further need of her, We married her to you, so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no further need of them. And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾ ﴿There is no discomfort for the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. [This is] the way of Allah with those who passed on before, and the command of Allah is a decree decreed.﴾ ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none but Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner.﴾ ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.﴾ ﴿And exalt Him morning and evening.﴾ ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [too], that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. And ever is He merciful to the believers.﴾ ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, "Peace," and He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner,﴾ ﴿And as one who invites to Allah by His permission and as a lamp giving light.﴾ ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah great bounty.﴾ ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾.

(p-233) The majority of scholars, Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, Mujahid and others said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed on behalf of Zayd the marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, but she refused and said, "I am not one to marry him." He said, "Yes, [you are]; so marry him, for I am pleased with him for you." She refused, and so this verse was revealed. It is mentioned that she and her brother ʿAbdullah disliked that, but when the verse was revealed, they were pleased. Ibn Zayd said: Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, who was the first woman to offer herself to the Prophet, gave herself to him, and he said, "I have accepted you and married you to Zayd ibn Harithah." She and her brother were displeased and said, "We only wanted him [the Prophet], yet he married us to his slave." So this verse was revealed. But the first cause is more sound. The connection of this verse is that when [Allah] mentioned those previous attributes of Islam and what follows, He followed that with what had proceeded from some of the Muslims, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicated a matter which some of them refused, and so they were rebuked, since obedience to him, peace be upon him, is obedience to Allah, and his command is His command.

Al-khiyarah (choice) is a verbal noun from takhayyara, contrary to the regular analogy, like al-tiyarah from tatayyara. It has also been read with a sukun on the ya, reported by ʿIsa ibn Sulayman. The two Harami readers, the two ʿIraqi readers (al-ʿArabiyyan), Abu Jaʿfar, Shaybah, al-Aʿraj and ʿIsa read "an takuna" with the feminine ta; (p-234) while the Kufans, al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash and al-Sulami read it with the ya. Since the phrase "li-mu'minin wa la mu'minah" is general in a negative context, the pronoun came plural according to meaning in His saying "lahum," giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine. Al-Zamakhshari said: The pronoun should have been singular, as you say: "ma ja'anee min rajulin wa la imra'atin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha" [No man or woman came to me but that it was of such a matter]. End. It is not as he mentioned, because this is a conjunction with waw, so it is not permissible to make the pronoun singular except by an implied ellipsis, i.e., "ma ja'anee min rajulin illa kana min sha'nihi kadha," and you say, "ma ja'a Zayd wa la ʿAmr illa darabā Khalidan" (neither Zayd nor ʿAmr came except that they struck Khalid); and it is not permissible to say "illa darab" except by ellipsis, as we have said.

﴿And when you said﴾ the address is to the Messenger, peace be upon him.

﴿to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour﴾ by Islam, which is the greatest blessing, and he is Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Messenger (ﷺ) had adopted.

﴿and you had bestowed favour on him﴾ which is his manumission; part of his story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾ and she is Zaynab bint Jahsh; it has been mentioned that the Messenger (ﷺ) had proposed her for him. It has also been said: Allah bestowed favour on him by your companionship and affection, and you bestowed favour on him by adopting him. "Zayd came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to separate from my companion. He said: 'Has something in her troubled you?' He said: No, by Allah, but she is haughty towards me because of her nobility, and she hurts me with her tongue. He said: '﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾,' meaning: do not divorce her, and it is a command of recommendation, '﴿and fear Allah﴾ in treating her well.' So he divorced her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her after the completion of her waiting period." He gave as the reason for his marrying her His saying: ﴿so that there would be no discomfort for the believers﴾ in marrying the wives of those whom they had adopted when they separate from them, and that these wives are not included in what was forbidden in His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [an-Nisa 23].

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn said: Allah had revealed to him that Zayd would divorce her, and that he would marry her by Allah's marrying her to him. When Zayd complained of her character and that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wished to divorce her, he said to him, "﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah﴾," by way of good manners and advice, while he knew that he would divorce her. This is what he concealed within himself, and he did not intend that he commanded him to divorce. When he knew that he would divorce her, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that a saying from the people would reach him about marrying Zaynab after Zayd, since he was his mawla, and he had commanded him to divorce her; so Allah rebuked him for this degree of [concern] in a matter which Allah had permitted, by saying "keep [your wife]" while knowing that he would divorce; so He informed him that Allah has more right to be feared, that is, in every situation. End. This report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn is what the researching commentators hold, such as al-Zuhri, Bakr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, al-Qushayri, the judge Abu Bakr ibn al-ʿArabi and others. What is meant by His saying: ﴿and you feared the people﴾ is only the slander of the hypocrites concerning the marriage of the wives of the Prophets, and the Prophet is protected in his movements and stillnesses.
